instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is used to show the  presence of a partly submerged object being towed?
Choice A: A diamond shape on the towed object Choice B: An all-round light at each end of the towed object Choice C: A searchlight from the towing vessel in the direction of the tow Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, a barge being towed astern must display ___________________.
Choice A: red and green sidelights only Choice B: a white sternlight only Choice C: sidelights and a sternlight Choice D: one all-round white light
response: Choice C: sidelights and a sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which signal is recognized as§a distress signal?
Choice A: Directing the beam of a searchlight at another vessel Choice B: A smoke signal giving off orange colored smoke Choice C: A whistle signal of one prolonged and three short blasts Choice D: International Code Signal "PAN" spoken over theradiotelephone
response: Choice B: A smoke signal giving off orange colored smoke

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is approaching a bend. You hear a prolonged blast from around the bend. You should _________________.
Choice A: back your engines Choice B: stop your engines and drift Choice C: answer with one prolonged blast Choice D: sound the danger signal
response: Choice C: answer with one prolonged blast

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you do NOT understand the course or intention of an approaching vessel you should  sound __________________.
Choice A: one short blast Choice B: one prolonged blast Choice C: not less than five short blasts Choice D: not less than five prolonged blasts
response: Choice C: not less than five short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation, you may take action to avoid  collision by your maneuver alone. When may this action be taken?
Choice A: At any time you feel it is appropriate Choice B: Only when you have reached extremis Choice C: When you determine that your present course will cross ahead of the other vessel Choice D: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action
response: Choice D: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your 15-meter tug is underway and crossing a deep and narrow channel. A large container vessel is off your port bow on a steady bearing. Which  statement is TRUE concerning this situation?
Choice A: You should maintain course and speed. Choice B: The container vessel is the stand-on as it is the  larger vessel. Choice C: You are not to impede the safe passage of the container  vessel in the channel. Choice D: None of the above
response: Choice C: You are not to impede the safe passage of the container  vessel in the channel.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If your vessel is underway in fog and you hear one prolonged and three short blasts, this is a _____________________.
Choice A: vessel not under command Choice B: sailing vessel Choice C: vessel being towed (manned) Choice D: vessel being towed (unmanned)
response: Choice C: vessel being towed (manned)

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel on pilotage duty at night will show sidelights and a sternlight ___________.
Choice A: when at anchor Choice B: only when making way Choice C: at any time when underway Choice D: only when the identifying lights are not being shown
response: Choice C: at any time when underway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel underway in fog making NO way must sound what signal?
Choice A: One long blast Choice B: Two prolonged blasts Choice C: One prolonged blast Choice D: One prolonged and two short blasts
response: Choice B: Two prolonged blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 95-meter vessel aground  sounds which fog signal?
Choice A: A rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds every two minutes Choice B: A whistle signal of one short, one prolonged, and one short blast Choice C: A prolonged blast of the whistle at intervals not to exceed one minute Choice D: A rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds, preceded and  followed by three separate and distinct strokes on the bell
response: Choice D: A rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds, preceded and  followed by three separate and distinct strokes on the bell

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel equipped with operational radar?
Choice A: She must use this equipment to obtain early warning of risk of collision. Choice B: The radar equipment is only required to be used in   restricted visibility. Choice C: The use of a radar excuses a vessel from the need of a  look-out. Choice D: The safe speed of such a vessel will likely be greater than that of vessels without radar.
response: Choice A: She must use this equipment to obtain early warning of risk of collision.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 200-meter vessel is aground in fog. Which signal is optional?
Choice A: A bell signal Choice B: A gong signal Choice C: A whistle signal Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: A whistle signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is a distress signal?
Choice A: A triangular flag above or below a ball Choice B: The International Code Signal of distress indicated by "JV" Choice C: A green smoke signal Choice D: Flames on the vessel as from a burning tar barrel
response: Choice D: Flames on the vessel as from a burning tar barrel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel must proceed at a safe speed _____.
Choice A: in restricted visibility Choice B: in congested waters Choice C: during darkness Choice D: at all times
response: Choice D: at all times

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A light signal of three flashes means _________________.
Choice A: "I am in doubt as to your actions" Choice B: "My engines are full speed astern" Choice C: "I desire to overtake you" Choice D: "I am operating astern propulsion"
response: Choice D: "I am operating astern propulsion"

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel underway may exhibit ___________________.
Choice A: a red light over a green light at the masthead Choice B: a green light over a red light at the masthead Choice C: two white lights in a vertical line at the stern Choice D: an all-round white light at the bow
response: Choice A: a red light over a green light at the masthead

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is overtaking a tug and tow as shown. Which statement is CORRECT?
Choice A: The sailing vessel is the stand-on vessel because it is  overtaking. Choice B: The sailing vessel is the stand-on vessel because it is  under sail. Choice C: The tug is the stand-on vessel because it is being   overtaken. Choice D: The tug is the stand-on vessel because it is towing.
response: Choice C: The tug is the stand-on vessel because it is being   overtaken.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The word "vessel", in the Rules, includes _____.
Choice A: sailing ships Choice B: nondisplacement craft Choice C: seaplanes Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel with the wind abaft the beam is navigating in fog. She should sound  ____________________.
Choice A: three short blasts Choice B: one prolonged blast Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts Choice D: two prolonged blasts
response: Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is a distress signal?
Choice A: Firing of green star shells Choice B: Sounding 5 short blasts on the whistle Choice C: Answering a one blast whistle signal with two blasts Choice D: A flaming barrel of oil on deck
response: Choice D: A flaming barrel of oil on deck

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If a towing vessel and her tow are severely restricted in their ability to change course, they may show lights in addition to their towing   identification lights. These additional lights may be shown if the tow is ________________.
Choice A: pushed ahead Choice B: towed alongside Choice C: towed astern Choice D: Any of the above
response: Choice D: Any of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If two sailing vessels are  running free with the wind on the same side, which one must keep clear of the other?
Choice A: The one with the wind closest abeam Choice B: The one with the wind closest astern Choice C: The one to leeward Choice D: The one to windward
response: Choice D: The one to windward

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY The masthead light may be  located at other than the fore and aft centerline on a power-driven vessel _________________.
Choice A: less than 20 meters in length Choice B: less than 12 meters in length Choice C: which has separate sidelights carried on the outboard  extremes of the vessel's breadth Choice D: engaged in fishing
response: Choice B: less than 12 meters in length

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The NAVIGATION RULES define a "vessel not under command" as a vessel which ______________.
Choice A: from the nature of her work is unable to keep out of the way of another vessel Choice B: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the rules Choice C: by taking action contrary to the rules has created a special circumstance situation Choice D: is moored, aground or anchored in a fairway
response: Choice B: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the rules

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Additional light signals are provided in the Annexes to the Rules for vessels __________.
Choice A: engaged in fishing Choice B: not under command Choice C: engaged in towing Choice D: under sail
response: Choice A: engaged in fishing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may combine her sidelights and sternlight in one lantern on the fore and aft centerline of the vessel?
Choice A: A 16-meter sailing vessel Choice B: A 25-meter power-driven vessel Choice C: A 28-meter sailing vessel Choice D: Any non-self-propelled vessel
response: Choice A: A 16-meter sailing vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The duration of a prolonged  blast of the whistle is __________________.
Choice A: 2 to 4 seconds Choice B: 4 to 6 seconds Choice C: 6 to 8 seconds Choice D: 8 to 10 seconds
response: Choice B: 4 to 6 seconds

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel "restricted in her  ability to maneuver" is one which _____.
Choice A: from the nature of her work is unable to maneuver as  required by the rules Choice B: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the rules Choice C: due to adverse weather conditions is unable to maneuver as required by the rules Choice D: has lost steering and is unable to maneuver
response: Choice A: from the nature of her work is unable to maneuver as  required by the rules

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When underway in restricted  visibility, you might hear, at intervals of two minutes, any of the following fog signals EXCEPT _________________.
Choice A: one prolonged blast Choice B: two prolonged blasts Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts Choice D: ringing of a bell for five seconds
response: Choice D: ringing of a bell for five seconds

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are preparing to cross a§narrow channel. You see a vessel that can only be navigated§safely within the channel. You should ___________.
Choice A: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel Choice B: initiate an exchange of passing signals Choice C: sound the danger signal Choice D: hold your course and speed
response: Choice A: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A bell is used to sound a fog signal for a _________________.
Choice A: power-driven vessel underway Choice B: sailing vessel at anchor Choice C: vessel engaged in fishing Choice D: vessel not under command
response: Choice B: sailing vessel at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see another vessel   approaching, and its compass bearing does not significantly change. This would indicate that _____.
Choice A: you are the stand-on vessel Choice B: risk of collision exists Choice C: a special circumstances situation exists Choice D: the other vessel is dead in the water
response: Choice B: risk of collision exists

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel pushing a barge ahead and rigidly connected in a composite unit shall show the lights of _________________.
Choice A: a vessel towing by pushing ahead Choice B: a power-driven vessel, not towing Choice C: a barge being pushed ahead Choice D: either answer A or answer B
response: Choice B: a power-driven vessel, not towing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are the watch officer on a power-driven vessel and notice a large sailing vessel  approaching from astern. You should _____.
Choice A: slow down Choice B: sound one short blast and change course to starboard Choice C: sound two short blasts and change course to port Choice D: hold your course and speed
response: Choice D: hold your course and speed

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel shall be deemed to§be overtaking when she can see at night ________.
Choice A: only the sternlight of the vessel Choice B: a sidelight and one masthead light of the vessel Choice C: only a sidelight of the vessel Choice D: any lights except the masthead lights of the vessel
response: Choice A: only the sternlight of the vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel trawling will display a ____________________.
Choice A: red light over a white light Choice B: green light over a white light Choice C: yellow light over a red light Choice D: white light over a green light
response: Choice B: green light over a white light

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If it becomes necessary for a stand-on vessel to take action to avoid collision, she  shall NOT, if possible, _____.
Choice A: decrease speed Choice B: increase speed Choice C: turn to port for a vessel on her own port side Choice D: turn to starboard for a vessel on her own port side
response: Choice C: turn to port for a vessel on her own port side

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is NOT making way, but is not in any way disabled. Another vessel is approaching you on your starboard beam. Which statement is TRUE?
Choice A: The other vessel must give way since your vessel is stopped. Choice B: Your vessel is the give-way vessel in a crossing situation. Choice C: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel not under command. Choice D: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel  restricted in her ability to maneuver.
response: Choice B: Your vessel is the give-way vessel in a crossing situation.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 22-meter sailing vessel when also being propelled by machinery shall show during daylight hours a _______________________.
Choice A: black diamond Choice B: black cone Choice C: black ball Choice D: basket
response: Choice B: black cone

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The rules concerning lights  shall be complied with in all weathers from sunset to  sunrise. The lights _____.
Choice A: shall be displayed in restricted visibility during daylight hours Choice B: need not be displayed when no other vessels are in the area Choice C: shall be set at low power when used during daylight hours Choice D: need not be displayed by unmanned vessels
response: Choice A: shall be displayed in restricted visibility during daylight hours

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Two vessels meeting in a "head- on" situation are directed by the Rules to ________________.
Choice A: alter course to starboard and pass port to port Choice B: alter course to port and pass starboard to starboard Choice C: decide on which side the passage will occur by matching  whistle signals Choice D: slow to bare steerageway
response: Choice A: alter course to starboard and pass port to port

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is "engaged in fishing" when ___________________.
Choice A: her gear extends more than 100 meters from the vessel Choice B: she is using any type of gear, other than lines Choice C: she is using fishing apparatus which restricts her   maneuverability Choice D: she has any fishing gear on board
response: Choice C: she is using fishing apparatus which restricts her   maneuverability

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When shall the stand-on vessel change course and speed?
Choice A: The stand-on vessel may change course and speed at any time as it has the right-of-way Choice B: After the give-way vessel sounds one blast in a crossing situation Choice C: When action by the give-way vessel alone cannot prevent  collision Choice D: When the two vessels become less than half a mile apart
response: Choice C: When action by the give-way vessel alone cannot prevent  collision

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel with the wind abaft the beam is navigating in restricted visibility. She should sound _________________.
Choice A: three short blasts Choice B: one prolonged blast Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts Choice D: two prolonged blasts
response: Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see a vessel displaying the§code flag "LIMA" below which is a red ball. The vessel is§_____.
Choice A: trolling Choice B: getting ready to receive aircraft Choice C: aground Choice D: in distress
response: Choice D: in distress

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which factor is listed in the Rules as one which must be taken into account when   determining safe speed?
Choice A: The construction of the vessel Choice B: The maneuverability of the vessel Choice C: The experience of vessel personnel Choice D: All of the above must be taken into account.
response: Choice B: The maneuverability of the vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning seaplanes on the water?
Choice A: A seaplane must show appropriate lights but need not exhibit shapes. Choice B: A seaplane should exhibit the lights for a vessel   constrained by her draft. Choice C: In situations where a risk of collision exists, a seaplane should always give way. Choice D: A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels.
response: Choice D: A seaplane on the water shall, in general, keep well clear of all vessels.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are in charge of a§power-driven vessel navigating at night. You sight the red§sidelight of another vessel on your port bow. The other§vessel's after masthead light is to the right of her forward§masthead light. You should _____.
Choice A: hold course and speed Choice B: alter course to port Choice C: stop engines Choice D: sound the danger signal
response: Choice A: hold course and speed

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND There are two classes of vessels which, to the extent necessary to carry out their work, do not have to comply with the rule regarding traffic   separation schemes. One of these is a vessel _____________.
Choice A: engaged in fishing in a traffic lane Choice B: servicing a submarine cable Choice C: towing another Choice D: engaged on pilotage duty
response: Choice B: servicing a submarine cable

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog when you hear the rapid ringing of a bell for five seconds followed by the sounding of a gong for five seconds. This signal indicates a vessel ___________________.
Choice A: aground Choice B: more than 100 meters in length, at anchor Choice C: fishing while making no way through the water Choice D: fishing in company with another vessel
response: Choice B: more than 100 meters in length, at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, which lights are  required to be shown by a dredge on the side of the dredge which another vessel may pass?
Choice A: One red light Choice B: Two red lights Choice C: One white light Choice D: Two green lights
response: Choice D: Two green lights

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which lights are shown by a  vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver to indicate that the vessel is making way?
Choice A: Masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight Choice B: Masthead lights and sidelights only Choice C: Sidelights and sternlight only Choice D: Sidelights only
response: Choice A: Masthead lights, sidelights and sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway and hear a  vessel continuously sounding her fog whistle. This   indicates the other vessel _________________.
Choice A: desires to communicate by radio Choice B: desires a pilot Choice C: is in distress Choice D: is aground
response: Choice C: is in distress

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 30-meter tug is underway and NOT towing. At night, this vessel must show sidelights and _____.
Choice A: one masthead light and a sternlight Choice B: two masthead lights and a sternlight Choice C: three masthead lights and a sternlight Choice D: a sternlight ONLY
response: Choice A: one masthead light and a sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a signal of one prolonged blast followed by three short  blasts. This is the fog signal for a vessel ___________.
Choice A: towing Choice B: manned being towed Choice C: unmanned being towed Choice D: at anchor
response: Choice B: manned being towed

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel of 75 meters in length, at anchor?
Choice A: She must show an all-round white light forward. Choice B: She must show a second all-round white light aft. Choice C: She may use her working lights to illuminate her decks. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another  vessel. She is about one mile distant and is on your  starboard bow. You believe she will cross ahead of   you. She then sounds a whistle signal of five    short blasts. You should _______________________.
Choice A: answer the signal and hold course and speed Choice B: reduce speed slightly to make sure she will have room to pass Choice C: make a large course change, and slow down if necessary Choice D: wait for another whistle signal from the other vessel
response: Choice C: make a large course change, and slow down if necessary

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If a rowboat underway does NOT show the lights specified for a sailing vessel underway, it shall show a _________________.
Choice A: white light from sunset to sunrise Choice B: combined lantern showing green to starboard and red to port and shown from sunset to sunrise Choice C: combined lantern showing green to starboard and red to port and shown in sufficient time to prevent collision Choice D: white light shown in sufficient time to prevent collision
response: Choice D: white light shown in sufficient time to prevent collision

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel at anchor shall  display, between sunrise and sunset, on the forward part of the vessel where it can best be seen ___________________.
Choice A: one black ball Choice B: two black balls Choice C: one red ball Choice D: two orange and white balls
response: Choice A: one black ball

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog and hear a fog signal of two prolonged blasts on your starboard  quarter. You should _____.
Choice A: stop your vessel Choice B: change course to the left Choice C: change course to the right Choice D: hold your course and speed
response: Choice D: hold your course and speed

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway, in fog, when you hear a whistle signal of one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts. This signal could indicate a vessel  ___________________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: being towed Choice C: aground Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: not under command

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must exhibit three white masthead lights in a vertical line?
Choice A: Any vessel towing astern Choice B: A vessel whose tow exceeds 200 meters astern Choice C: A vessel not under command, at anchor Choice D: A vessel being towed
response: Choice B: A vessel whose tow exceeds 200 meters astern

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND All of the following are  distress signals EXCEPT _________________.
Choice A: the continuous sounding of any fog signal apparatus Choice B: giving five or more short and rapid blasts of the whistle Choice C: firing a gun at intervals of about a minute Choice D: a barrel with burning oil in it, on deck
response: Choice B: giving five or more short and rapid blasts of the whistle

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you are approaching a bend, and hear a whistle signal of one prolonged blast from around the bend, you should answer with a signal of _____________.
Choice A: a short blast Choice B: a prolonged blast Choice C: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast Choice D: a long blast
response: Choice B: a prolonged blast

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must show an after masthead light, if over 50 meters in length?
Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing Choice B: A vessel at anchor Choice C: A vessel not under command Choice D: A vessel trawling
response: Choice D: A vessel trawling

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A "flashing light", by the  definition given in the rules, is a light that _______.
Choice A: is red in color Choice B: is visible over an arc of the horizon of 360° Choice C: flashes at regular intervals at a frequency of 120 flashes or more per minute Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: flashes at regular intervals at a frequency of 120 flashes or more per minute

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The term "restricted visibility" as used in the Rules refers ___________________.
Choice A: only to fog Choice B: only to visibility of less than one-half of a mile Choice C: to visibility where you cannot see shore Choice D: to any condition where visibility is restricted
response: Choice D: to any condition where visibility is restricted

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND A vessel engaged in   mineclearing shows special identity lights _____.
Choice A: in addition to the lights required for a power-driven vessel Choice B: which mean that other vessels should not approach within 1000 meters of the mineclearing vessel Choice C: which are green and show all-round Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND According to the Navigation  Rules, you may depart from the Rules when _______________.
Choice A: no vessels are in sight visually Choice B: no vessels are visible on radar Choice C: you are in immediate danger Choice D: out of sight of land
response: Choice C: you are in immediate danger

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An authorized light to assist in the identification of submarines operating on the surface is a(n) ________________.
Choice A: blue rotating light Choice B: intermittent flashing amber/yellow light Choice C: flashing white light Choice D: flashing sidelight
response: Choice B: intermittent flashing amber/yellow light

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning two sailing vessels?
Choice A: A sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on her port side shall keep out of the way of a sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on the starboard side. Choice B: When both vessels have the wind on the same side, the vessel to leeward shall keep out of the way. Choice C: A sail vessel with the wind abaft of the beam must keep out of the way of a vessel sailing into the wind. Choice D: None of the above
response: Choice A: A sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on her port side shall keep out of the way of a sailing vessel with the wind forward of the beam on the starboard side.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When underway in a channel, you should keep to the _____.
Choice A: middle of the channel Choice B: starboard side of the channel Choice C: port side of the channel Choice D: side of the channel that has the widest turns
response: Choice B: starboard side of the channel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway, in fog, you hear a whistle signal of one prolonged blast followed by two  short blasts. This signal is sounded by a vessel   ___________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: being towed Choice C: on pilotage duty Choice D: aground
response: Choice A: not under command

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When navigating in restricted visibility, a power-driven vessel shall ________________.
Choice A: stop her engines when hearing a fog signal forward of her beam, even if risk of collision does not exist Choice B: have her engines ready for immediate maneuver Choice C: when making way, sound one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than one minute Choice D: operate at a speed to be able to stop in the distance of her visibility
response: Choice B: have her engines ready for immediate maneuver

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You can indicate that your  vessel is in distress by ___________________.
Choice A: displaying a large red flag Choice B: displaying three black balls in a vertical line Choice C: sounding four or more short rapid blasts on the whistle Choice D: continuously sounding the fog whistle
response: Choice D: continuously sounding the fog whistle

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND During the day, a dredge will indicate the side on which it is safe to pass by displaying _________________.
Choice A: two balls in a vertical line Choice B: two diamonds in a vertical line Choice C: a single black ball Choice D: no shape is shown during the day
response: Choice B: two diamonds in a vertical line

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 45-meter vessel is pulling a 210-meter tow. She may exhibit ________________.
Choice A: a masthead light forward, and two masthead lights in a  vertical line aft Choice B: three masthead lights forward and one aft Choice C: two masthead lights forward and no after masthead light Choice D: three masthead lights aft and none forward
response: Choice B: three masthead lights forward and one aft

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is§TRUE concerning the danger signal?
Choice A: When any vessel fails to understand the intentions of an approaching vessel she must sound the danger signal. Choice B: Only the stand-on vessel can sound the danger signal. Choice C: Distress signals may be used in place of the danger signal. Choice D: The danger signal consists of 4 or more short blasts of the whistle.
response: Choice A: When any vessel fails to understand the intentions of an approaching vessel she must sound the danger signal.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A distress signal _____________.
Choice A: consists of 5 or more short blasts of the fog signal  apparatus Choice B: may be used separately or with other distress signals Choice C: consists of the raising and lowering of a large white flag Choice D: is used to indicate doubt about another vessel's intentions
response: Choice B: may be used separately or with other distress signals

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is the danger signal?
Choice A: A continuous sounding of the fog signal Choice B: Firing a gun every minute Choice C: Five or more short rapid blasts on the whistle Choice D: One prolonged blast on the whistle
response: Choice C: Five or more short rapid blasts on the whistle

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is "in sight" of  another vessel when ___________________.
Choice A: she can be observed by radar Choice B: she can be observed visually from the other vessel Choice C: she can be plotted on radar well enough to determine her heading Choice D: her fog signal can be heard
response: Choice B: she can be observed visually from the other vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning two sailing vessels approaching each other?
Choice A: A sailing vessel overtaking another is the give-way vessel. Choice B: When each is on a different tack, the vessel on the   starboard tack shall keep out of the way. Choice C: A sailing vessel seeing another to leeward on an   undetermined tack shall hold her course. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: A sailing vessel overtaking another is the give-way vessel.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What type of vessel or operation is indicated by a vessel showing two cones with the apexes together?
Choice A: Sailing vessel Choice B: Vessel trawling Choice C: Mineclearing Choice D: Dredge
response: Choice B: Vessel trawling

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel has on her port side a sailing vessel which is on a collision course. The power-driven vessel is to ___________________.
Choice A: maintain course and speed Choice B: keep clear, passing at a safe distance Choice C: sound one blast and turn to starboard Choice D: stop her engines
response: Choice B: keep clear, passing at a safe distance

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At specified intervals, a vessel towing in fog shall sound _________________.
Choice A: one prolonged blast Choice B: two prolonged blasts Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts in succession Choice D: one prolonged and three short blasts in succession
response: Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts in succession

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing in fog shall sound a fog signal of _________________.
Choice A: one prolonged blast every one minute Choice B: two prolonged blasts every two minutes Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts every two minutes Choice D: one prolonged blast every two minutes
response: Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts every two minutes

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Continuous sounding of a fog whistle by a vessel is a signal ___________________.
Choice A: that the vessel is anchored Choice B: to request the draw span of a bridge to be opened Choice C: of distress Choice D: that the vessel is broken down and drifting
response: Choice C: of distress

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND A 50-meter vessel is towing astern and the length of the tow is 100 meters. In addition to sidelights, which lights may she show to fully comply with the Rules?
Choice A: Two masthead lights forward, a sternlight, and a towing  light above the sternlight Choice B: A masthead light forward, two masthead lights aft, a  sternlight, and a towing light above the sternlight Choice C: No masthead light forward, two masthead lights aft, a  sternlight, and a towing light above the sternlight Choice D: Three masthead lights forward, one masthead light aft, and two towing lights in a vertical line at the stern
response: Choice B: A masthead light forward, two masthead lights aft, a  sternlight, and a towing light above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel, which is unable to maneuver due to some exceptional circumstance, shall exhibit ___________________.
Choice A: during the day, three balls in a vertical line Choice B: during the day, three shapes, the highest and lowest being balls and the middle being a diamond Choice C: when making way at night, two all-round red lights,   sidelights, and a sternlight Choice D: when making way at night, masthead lights, sidelights, and a sternlight
response: Choice C: when making way at night, two all-round red lights,   sidelights, and a sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which signal, other than a  distress signal, can be used by a vessel to attract   attention?
Choice A: Searchlight beam Choice B: Continuous sounding of a fog signal apparatus Choice C: Burning barrel Choice D: Orange smoke signal
response: Choice A: Searchlight beam

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning the light used with whistle signals?
Choice A: Use of such a light is required. Choice B: The light shall have the same characteristics as a masthead light. Choice C: It is only used to supplement short blasts of the whistle. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: It is only used to supplement short blasts of the whistle.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum sound  signaling equipment required aboard a vessel 14 meters in length?
Choice A: A bell only Choice B: A whistle only Choice C: A bell and a whistle Choice D: Any means of making an efficient sound signal
response: Choice C: A bell and a whistle

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The towing light is a(n) ______.
Choice A: flashing amber light Choice B: yellow light with the same characteristics as the sternlight Choice C: all-round yellow light Choice D: yellow light with the same characteristics as the masthead light
response: Choice B: yellow light with the same characteristics as the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An all-round flashing yellow light may be exhibited by a(n) _________________.
Choice A: vessel not under command Choice B: air cushion vessel in the nondisplacement mode Choice C: vessel towing a submerged object Choice D: vessel engaged in diving operations
response: Choice B: air cushion vessel in the nondisplacement mode

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When should the fog signal of a manned vessel under tow be sounded?
Choice A: After the towing vessel's fog signal Choice B: Before the towing vessel's fog signal Choice C: Approximately one minute after the towing vessel's fog  signal Choice D: If the towing vessel is sounding a fog signal, the   manned vessel being towed is not required to sound any fog signal.
response: Choice A: After the towing vessel's fog signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A lantern combining a vessel's navigation lights may be shown on a ________________.
Choice A: 15-meter sailing vessel Choice B: 20-meter vessel engaged in fishing and making way Choice C: 25-meter power-driven vessel trolling Choice D: 25-meter pilot vessel
response: Choice A: 15-meter sailing vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  during the day would show _______________.
Choice A: one black ball Choice B: two cones with bases together Choice C: a cone, apex downward Choice D: two cones, apexes together
response: Choice D: two cones, apexes together

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is NOT required to keep out of the way of a _____________________.
Choice A: power-driven vessel Choice B: vessel not under command Choice C: vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice D: vessel engaged in fishing
response: Choice A: power-driven vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may sound the  danger signal?
Choice A: The stand-on vessel in a crossing situation Choice B: The give-way vessel in a crossing situation Choice C: A vessel at anchor Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel sound one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts on the whistle. What does this signal indicate?
Choice A: A vessel towing Choice B: A vessel engaged in pilotage duty Choice C: A vessel being towed Choice D: A vessel aground
response: Choice A: A vessel towing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you saw flames aboard a  vessel but could see the vessel was not on fire, you would know that the _____.
Choice A: crew was trying to get warm Choice B: vessel required immediate assistance Choice C: vessel was attempting to attract the attention of a pilot boat Choice D: vessel was being illuminated for identification by aircraft
response: Choice B: vessel required immediate assistance

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND By day, when it is impracticable for a small vessel engaged in diving operations to display the shapes for a vessel engaged in underwater operations, she shall display ___________________.
Choice A: three black balls in a vertical line Choice B: two red balls in a vertical line Choice C: a black cylinder Choice D: a rigid replica of the International Code flag "A"
response: Choice D: a rigid replica of the International Code flag "A"

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel will NOT show   sidelights when _________________.
Choice A: underway but not making way Choice B: making way, not under command Choice C: not under command, not making way Choice D: trolling underway
response: Choice C: not under command, not making way

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which display indicates a vessel conducting mineclearance operations?
Choice A: Three balls in a vertical line Choice B: Two balls in a vertical line Choice C: One ball near the foremast and one ball at each yardarm Choice D: One diamond near the foremast and one ball at each yardarm
response: Choice C: One ball near the foremast and one ball at each yardarm

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel MUST show two  masthead lights in a vertical line?
Choice A: A power-driven vessel less than 50 meters in length with a 20-meter tow Choice B: A sailing vessel towing a small vessel astern Choice C: A vessel not under command Choice D: A vessel engaged in dredging
response: Choice A: A power-driven vessel less than 50 meters in length with a 20-meter tow

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The duration of each blast of the whistle signals used in meeting and crossing situations is _________________.
Choice A: about 1 second Choice B: 2 or 4 seconds Choice C: 4 to 6 seconds Choice D: 8 to 10 seconds
response: Choice A: about 1 second

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What dayshape should a vessel being towed exhibit if the tow EXCEEDS 200 meters?
Choice A: Two balls Choice B: Two diamonds Choice C: One ball Choice D: One diamond
response: Choice D: One diamond

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE when you are towing more than one barge astern at night?
Choice A: Only the last barge in the tow must be lighted. Choice B: Only the first and last barges in the tow must be lighted. Choice C: All barges in the tow must be lighted. Choice D: All barges, except unmanned barges, must be lighted.
response: Choice C: All barges in the tow must be lighted.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel is being propelled both by sail and by engines. Under the Rules, the vessel is  ________________.
Choice A: a "special circumstance" vessel Choice B: not covered under any category Choice C: a sail vessel Choice D: a power-driven vessel
response: Choice D: a power-driven vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The white masthead light  required for a power-driven vessel under the Rules is  visible over how many degrees of the horizon?
Choice A: 022.5° Choice B: 112.5° Choice C: 225.0° Choice D: 360.0°
response: Choice C: 225.0°

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning lights and shapes for towing vessels?
Choice A: If a tow exceeds 200 meters in length, the towing vessel will display a black ball during daylight. Choice B: When towing astern, a vessel will carry her identification lights at the masthead in addition to her regular masthead light. Choice C: When towing astern, the towing vessel may show either a  sternlight or a towing light, but not both. Choice D: If the towing vessel is over 50 meters in length, she must carry forward and after masthead lights.
response: Choice D: If the towing vessel is over 50 meters in length, she must carry forward and after masthead lights.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel may use any sound or light signals to attract the attention of another vessel as long as ___________________.
Choice A: white lights are not used Choice B: red and green lights are not used Choice C: the vessel signals such intentions over the radiotelephone Choice D: the signal cannot be mistaken for a signal authorized by the Rules
response: Choice D: the signal cannot be mistaken for a signal authorized by the Rules

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What type of vessel or operation is indicated by a vessel displaying two cones with the  apexes together?
Choice A: Sailing Choice B: Trawling Choice C: Minesweeping Choice D: Dredging
response: Choice B: Trawling

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The rule regarding look-outs applies _____________________.
Choice A: in restricted visibility Choice B: between dusk and dawn Choice C: in heavy traffic Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway and towing, your vessel enters fog. Which fog signal should you sound?
Choice A: One prolonged blast Choice B: Two prolonged blasts Choice C: One prolonged blast and two short blasts Choice D: Three distinct blasts
response: Choice C: One prolonged blast and two short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing must display a light in the direction of any gear that extends outward more than 150 meters. The color of this light is _________________.
Choice A: white Choice B: green Choice C: red Choice D: yellow
response: Choice A: white

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is true   concerning a towing light when a towing vessel is towing astern?
Choice A: When a towing light is shown, no sternlight is necessary. Choice B: When a sternlight is shown, no towing light is necessary. Choice C: The towing light is shown below the sternlight. Choice D: The towing light is shown above the sternlight.
response: Choice D: The towing light is shown above the sternlight.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, a vessel which is less than 7 meters in length and anchored in an area where other vessels do not normally navigate is ___________________.
Choice A: not required to show any anchor lights Choice B: required to show a flare-up light Choice C: required to show one white light Choice D: required to show sidelights and a sternlight
response: Choice A: not required to show any anchor lights

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are in charge of a 120-meter power-driven vessel at anchor in fog, sounding the required anchor signals. You hear the fog signal of a vessel  underway off your port bow. You may sound _______________.
Choice A: at least five short and rapid blasts Choice B: two short blasts Choice C: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast Choice D: three short blasts
response: Choice C: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When taking action to avoid  collision, you should ___________________.
Choice A: make sure the action is taken in enough time Choice B: not make any large course changes Choice C: not make any large speed changes Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: make sure the action is taken in enough time

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would have no white lights visible when meeting her head-on?
Choice A: A vessel trawling Choice B: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: A vessel mineclearing Choice D: A vessel not under command
response: Choice D: A vessel not under command

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are in restricted visibility and hear a fog signal forward of the beam. Nothing appears on your radar screen. You must ___________.
Choice A: stop your engines Choice B: sound two prolonged blasts of the whistle Choice C: sound the danger signal Choice D: slow to bare steerageway
response: Choice D: slow to bare steerageway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel 30 meters in length is pushing barges ahead. How many white masthead lights is the vessel REQUIRED to show at night?
Choice A: One Choice B: Two Choice C: Three Choice D: Four
response: Choice B: Two

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog you hear a vessel sound one prolonged blast followed by two short  blasts. What does this signal indicate?
Choice A: A vessel towing Choice B: A vessel being towed Choice C: A pilot vessel engaged on pilotage duty Choice D: A vessel aground
response: Choice A: A vessel towing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel with a 150-meter stern tow shall display _____.
Choice A: three masthead lights in a vertical line Choice B: a towing light above the sternlight Choice C: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice D: a red light over a white light at the masthead
response: Choice B: a towing light above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel transferring cargo  while underway is classified by the Rules as a vessel  _________________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: in special circumstances Choice C: restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice D: constrained by her draft
response: Choice C: restricted in her ability to maneuver

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel, when anchored at night, is NOT required to show anchor lights?
Choice A: A power-driven vessel Choice B: A vessel engaged on pilotage duty Choice C: A vessel dredging Choice D: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver
response: Choice C: A vessel dredging

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing is showing three forward white masthead lights in a vertical line. This  means that the length of the ________________.
Choice A: towing vessel is less than 50 meters Choice B: towing vessel is greater than 50 meters Choice C: tow is less than 200 meters Choice D: tow is greater than 200 meters
response: Choice D: tow is greater than 200 meters

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is "underway" under the Rules of the Road?
Choice A: A vessel at anchor with the engine running Choice B: A vessel with a line led to a tree onshore Choice C: A vessel drifting with the engine off Choice D: A vessel aground
response: Choice C: A vessel drifting with the engine off

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may exhibit  identifying lights when not actually engaged in her   occupation?
Choice A: A trawler Choice B: A fishing vessel Choice C: A tug Choice D: None of the above
response: Choice D: None of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 25-meter vessel trawling will show the dayshape(s) consisting of _______________.
Choice A: a basket Choice B: two balls Choice C: two cones, apexes together Choice D: a cone, apex downward
response: Choice C: two cones, apexes together

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a _________________.
Choice A: vessel not under command Choice B: vessel engaged in fishing Choice C: sailing vessel Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fog signal of one short, one prolonged, and one short blast may be sounded by a ________.
Choice A: vessel at anchor Choice B: vessel not under command Choice C: vessel towing Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: vessel at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A continuous sounding of a  fog-signal apparatus indicates _____.
Choice A: the vessel is in distress Choice B: the vessel has completed loading dangerous cargo Choice C: it is safe to pass Choice D: the vessel is anchored
response: Choice A: the vessel is in distress

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in restricted§visibility. You hear the fog signal of another vessel about§22° on your starboard bow. If danger of collision exists§you must __________.
Choice A: reduce your speed to bare steerageway Choice B: slow your engines and let the other vessel pass ahead of you Choice C: alter the course to starboard to pass around the other vessel's stern Choice D: alter course to port to pass the other vessle on its port side
response: Choice A: reduce your speed to bare steerageway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog you hear a whistle signal consisting of one prolonged blast followed immediately by two short blasts. This signal is sounded in fog by _________________.
Choice A: vessels at anchor, not engaged in fishing Choice B: vessels underway and towing Choice C: vessels in danger Choice D: pilot vessels
response: Choice B: vessels underway and towing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE of a 30-meter sailing vessel underway?
Choice A: She must show sidelights and a sternlight in restricted  visibility. Choice B: She may show an all-round white light at the top of the  mast. Choice C: She need not show a sternlight if she is showing all-round lights on the mast. Choice D: If she is using propelling machinery, she shall show forward a shape consisting of two cones, apexes together.
response: Choice A: She must show sidelights and a sternlight in restricted  visibility.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel towing another vessel astern (tow less than 200 meters) shall show _______________.
Choice A: three masthead lights in a vertical line instead of   either the forward or after masthead light Choice B: two masthead lights in a vertical line instead of either the forward or after masthead lights Choice C: two towing lights in a vertical line at the stern Choice D: a small white light aft of the funnel
response: Choice B: two masthead lights in a vertical line instead of either the forward or after masthead lights

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel which is "restricted in her ability to maneuver" under the Rules, is a vessel which is _____________________.
Choice A: mineclearing Choice B: engaged in fishing Choice C: at anchor Choice D: not under command
response: Choice A: mineclearing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When a vessel signals her  distress by means of a gun or other explosive signal, the firing should be at intervals of approximately _____.
Choice A: 10 minutes Choice B: 1 minute Choice C: 1 hour Choice D: 3 minutes
response: Choice B: 1 minute

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A "head on" situation shall be§deemed to exist at night when a power-driven vessel sees another power-driven vessel ahead and _________________.
Choice A: one sidelight and the masthead light are visible Choice B: the vessels will pass closer than half a mile Choice C: both vessels sound one prolonged blast Choice D: both sidelights and masthead light(s) are visible
response: Choice D: both sidelights and masthead light(s) are visible

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 20-meter vessel is towing  another vessel astern. The length of the tow from the stern of the towing vessel to the stern of the tow is 75 meters. How many white towing masthead lights shall the towing  vessel show at night?
Choice A: 1 Choice B: 2 Choice C: 3 Choice D: 4
response: Choice B: 2

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel enagaged in fishing,§and at anchor, shall show _____________.
Choice A: an anchor light Choice B: sidelights and a sternlight Choice C: three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest  being red, and the middle being white Choice D: None of the above
response: Choice D: None of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a vessel _______________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: engaged in fishing Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel sounding a fog signal of one short, one prolonged, and one short blast is   indicating that the vessel is _______________.
Choice A: fishing Choice B: in distress Choice C: at anchor Choice D: not under command
response: Choice C: at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Two all-round red lights§displayed in a vertical line are shown by a vessel ________.
Choice A: being towed Choice B: pushing a barge ahead Choice C: at anchor Choice D: not under command
response: Choice D: not under command

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is underway in§reduced visibility. You hear the fog signal of another§vessel about 30‚ on your starboard bow. If danger of§collision exists, you must _______.
Choice A: alter course to starboard to pass around the other vessel's stern Choice B: slow your engines and let the other vessel pass ahead of you Choice C: reduce your speed to bare steerageway Choice D: alter course to port and pass the other vessel on its port side
response: Choice C: reduce your speed to bare steerageway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog and you hear one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts. This is a vessel _________________.
Choice A: towing Choice B: engaged on pilotage duty Choice C: aground in a fairway Choice D: stopped and making no way through the water
response: Choice A: towing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel is NOT allowed to show the all-round red over green lights on the mast if __________________.
Choice A: she is showing sidelights Choice B: her sidelights are combined and shown on the fore and aft centerline of the vessel Choice C: she is showing a sternlight Choice D: her sidelights and sternlight are combined in one lantern and shown on the mast
response: Choice D: her sidelights and sternlight are combined in one lantern and shown on the mast

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel, when  towing astern, shall show _____.
Choice A: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight Choice C: two towing lights in addition to the sternlight Choice D: a small white light in lieu of the sternlight
response: Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND According to the Rules, which vessel is NOT "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Choice A: A vessel servicing a navigation marker Choice B: A sailing vessel Choice C: A vessel mineclearing Choice D: A vessel dredging
response: Choice B: A sailing vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Distress signals may be _____.
Choice A: red flares Choice B: smoke signals Choice C: sound signals Choice D: Any of the above
response: Choice D: Any of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When anchoring a 25-meter vessel at night, you must show __________________.
Choice A: one all-round white light Choice B: two all-round white lights Choice C: one all-round white light and the sidelights Choice D: the sidelights and a sternlight
response: Choice A: one all-round white light

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another  vessel at night. You can see both red and green sidelights and, above the level of the sidelights, three white lights in a vertical line. The vessel may be _________________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: towing a tow more than 200 meters astern Choice C: trawling Choice D: underway and dredging
response: Choice B: towing a tow more than 200 meters astern

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing, and at anchor, should exhibit _____.
Choice A: an anchor light Choice B: sidelights and sternlight Choice C: three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest  being red, and the middle being white Choice D: None of the above
response: Choice D: None of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation on open waters, a sailing vessel shall keep out of the way of all the following vessels EXCEPT a ___________________.
Choice A: vessel not under command Choice B: vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: power-driven vessel approaching on her starboard side Choice D: vessel fishing
response: Choice C: power-driven vessel approaching on her starboard side

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are at anchor in fog on a§120-meter power-driven vessel. You hear the fog signal of§a vessel approaching off your port bow. You may sound ____.
Choice A: one prolonged, one short and one prolonged Choice B: two short blasts Choice C: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast Choice D: one prolonged blast
response: Choice C: one short, one prolonged, and one short blast

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds a fog signal of ________________.
Choice A: one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two  minutes Choice B: two prolonged blasts at intervals of not more than two  minutes Choice C: one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than one  minute Choice D: two prolonged blasts at intervals of not more than one  minute
response: Choice A: one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two  minutes

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are on watch in the fog. Your vessel is proceeding at a safe speed when you hear a fog signal ahead of you. The Rules require you to navigate with caution and, if danger of collision exists, _________.
Choice A: slow to less than 2 knots Choice B: stop your engines Choice C: reduce to bare steerageway Choice D: begin a radar plot
response: Choice C: reduce to bare steerageway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In restricted visibility, a  vessel fishing with nets shall sound at intervals of two minutes ________________.
Choice A: one prolonged blast Choice B: one prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice C: one prolonged followed by three short blasts Choice D: two prolonged blasts in succession
response: Choice B: one prolonged followed by two short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 20-meter sailing vessel  underway must exhibit a _______________.
Choice A: sternlight Choice B: combined lantern Choice C: red light over a green light at the masthead Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night, you are towing a  partly submerged vessel, 20 meters in length and 4 meters in breadth. What lights must you display on the towed vessel?
Choice A: A white light at the stern Choice B: Two white lights side by side at the stern Choice C: A white light at the forward end and a white light at the after end Choice D: Two red lights in a vertical line at the after end
response: Choice C: A white light at the forward end and a white light at the after end

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND All of the following vessels are "restricted in their ability to maneuver" EXCEPT a vessel ___________________.
Choice A: laying a pipeline Choice B: dredging Choice C: mineclearing Choice D: not under command
response: Choice D: not under command

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What lights must be shown on a barge being towed astern at night?
Choice A: A white light at each corner Choice B: A white light fore and aft Choice C: Sidelights and a sternlight Choice D: A sternlight only
response: Choice C: Sidelights and a sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel which is unable to  maneuver due to some exceptional circumstance, shall show two red lights in a vertical line and ___________________.
Choice A: during the day, three balls in a vertical line Choice B: during the day, three shapes, the highest and lowest being balls and the middle being a diamond Choice C: when making way at night, sidelights and a sternlight Choice D: when making way at night, masthead lights, sidelights, and a sternlight
response: Choice C: when making way at night, sidelights and a sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway and approaching a bend in the channel where vessels approaching from the opposite direction cannot be seen. You should sound ______.
Choice A: one blast, 4 to 6 seconds in duration Choice B: three blasts, 4 to 6 seconds in duration Choice C: one continuous blast until you are able to see around the bend Choice D: one blast, 8 to 10 seconds in duration
response: Choice A: one blast, 4 to 6 seconds in duration

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel which is fishing must show sidelights and a sternlight only when _______________.
Choice A: anchored Choice B: underway Choice C: dead in the water Choice D: underway and making way
response: Choice D: underway and making way

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel towing astern shall show _____.
Choice A: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight Choice C: two towing lights in addition to the sternlight Choice D: a small white light in lieu of the sternlight
response: Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in fog when you hear the following signal: one short blast, one prolonged blast and one short blast in succession. Which of the  following would it be?
Choice A: A sailing vessel underway with the wind abaft the beam Choice B: A power-driven vessel underway and making way through the water Choice C: A vessel at anchor Choice D: A vessel towing
response: Choice C: A vessel at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you hear the firing of a gun at one minute intervals from another vessel, this indicates that ___________________.
Choice A: the gun is being used to sound passing signals Choice B: the vessel is in distress Choice C: all vessels are to clear the area Choice D: all is clear and it is safe to pass
response: Choice B: the vessel is in distress

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Fog signals, required under the Rules for vessels underway, shall be sounded ______________.
Choice A: only on the approach of another vessel Choice B: only when vessels are in sight of each other Choice C: at intervals of not more than one minute Choice D: at intervals of not more than two minutes

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

response: Choice D: sternlight

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

response: Choice B: Proper use shall be made of radar equipment to determine risk of collision.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are fishing at night, and you sight a vessel showing three lights in a vertical line. The upper and lower lights are red and the middle light is white. Which statement is TRUE?

response: Choice A: You must keep out of the way of the other vessel.

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

Choice A: A vessel not under command Choice B: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice C: A vessel underway in fog Choice D: A vessel towing unable to deviate from her course
response: Choice D: A vessel towing unable to deviate from her course

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching another vessel and are not sure whether danger of collision exists. You must assume ______________.

response: Choice A: there is risk of collision

instruction:

response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:

instruction:

response: Choice C: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible.

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

response: Choice B: 67.5°

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

instruction:

response: Choice A: state of wind, sea, and current, and the proximity of  navigational hazards

instruction:
