response: Choice C: A vessel dredging

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel not under command shall display ____________________.
Choice A: two red lights at night and two black balls during daylight Choice B: two red lights at night and three black balls during  daylight Choice C: three red lights at night and two black balls during  daylight Choice D: three red lights at night and three black balls during  daylight
response: Choice A: two red lights at night and two black balls during daylight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  while at anchor shall sound a fog signal of _____.
Choice A: one prolonged and two short blasts at two-minute intervals Choice B: one prolonged and three short blasts at two-minute   intervals Choice C: a rapid ringing of the bell for five seconds at one-minute intervals Choice D: a sounding of the bell and gong at one-minute intervals
response: Choice A: one prolonged and two short blasts at two-minute intervals

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Underway at night you see the red sidelight of a vessel well off your port bow. Which statement is TRUE?
Choice A: You are required to alter course to the right. Choice B: You must stop engines. Choice C: You are on a collision course with the other vessel. Choice D: You may maintain course and speed.
response: Choice D: You may maintain course and speed.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would sound a fog signal consisting of the ringing of a bell for 5 seconds?
Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing, at anchor Choice B: A vessel restricted in its ability to maneuver, at anchor Choice C: A sailing vessel, at anchor Choice D: A sailing vessel becalmed
response: Choice C: A sailing vessel, at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel towing a barge astern would show, at the stern ___________________.
Choice A: only a sternlight Choice B: a towing light above the sternlight Choice C: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice D: two white lights in a vertical line
response: Choice B: a towing light above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fog signal consisting of one prolonged blast followed by four short blasts would indicate the presence of a ___________________.
Choice A: vessel being towed Choice B: fishing vessel engaged in trawling Choice C: vessel at anchor warning of her location Choice D: power-driven pilot vessel on station underway
response: Choice D: power-driven pilot vessel on station underway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In addition to sidelights what light should a vessel being towed astern show?
Choice A: A sternlight Choice B: A masthead light Choice C: Not under command lights Choice D: Range lights
response: Choice A: A sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel may continue to sound an identity signal if she is ___________________.
Choice A: aground Choice B: at anchor Choice C: not under command Choice D: being towed
response: Choice B: at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on and there is a risk of collision, each shall _______________.
Choice A: stop her engines Choice B: alter course to starboard Choice C: sound the danger signal Choice D: back down
response: Choice B: alter course to starboard

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power driven vessel when§towing and the length of the tow exceeds 200 meters shall§exhibit during daylight hours where they can best be§seen which of the following shapes?
Choice A: a diamond shape Choice B: two cones, apexes together Choice C: a black ball Choice D: one cone, apex upward
response: Choice A: a diamond shape

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum length of vessels required to show two anchor lights?
Choice A: 40 meters Choice B: 50 meters Choice C: 60 meters Choice D: 70 meters
response: Choice B: 50 meters

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel showing a rigid replica of the International Code flag "A" is engaged in __________.
Choice A: diving operations Choice B: dredging Choice C: fishing Choice D: mineclearance operations
response: Choice A: diving operations

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In determining "safe speed", all of the following must be taken into account EXCEPT the  _______________.
Choice A: maximum horsepower of your vessel Choice B: presence of background lights at night Choice C: draft of your vessel Choice D: maneuverability of your vessel
response: Choice A: maximum horsepower of your vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are aboard the give-way  vessel in a crossing situation. What should you NOT do in obeying the Rules?
Choice A: Cross ahead of the stand-on vessel Choice B: Make a large course change to starboard Choice C: Slow your vessel Choice D: Back your vessel
response: Choice A: Cross ahead of the stand-on vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel, which does not  normally engage in towing operations, is towing a vessel in distress. She ___________________.
Choice A: need not show the lights for a vessel engaged in towing, if it is impractical to do so Choice B: may show the lights for a vessel not under command Choice C: must show a yellow light above the sternlight Choice D: must show the lights for a vessel towing
response: Choice A: need not show the lights for a vessel engaged in towing, if it is impractical to do so

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND An all-round flashing yellow light may be exhibited by a(n) __________________.
Choice A: vessel laying cable Choice B: vessel towing a submerged object Choice C: vessel not under command Choice D: air cushion vessel
response: Choice D: air cushion vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Working lights shall be used to illuminate the decks of a vessel ___________________.
Choice A: over 100 meters at anchor Choice B: not under command Choice C: constrained by her draft Choice D: Any of the above
response: Choice A: over 100 meters at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may show   identifying lights when not actually engaged in her   occupation?
Choice A: A fishing vessel Choice B: A pilot vessel Choice C: A mineclearance vessel Choice D: None of the above
response: Choice D: None of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A pilot vessel may continue to sound an identity signal if she is ___________________.
Choice A: underway, but not making way Choice B: aground Choice C: being towed Choice D: not engaged in pilotage duty
response: Choice A: underway, but not making way

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If your vessel is the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation _____.
Choice A: you must keep your course and speed Choice B: you may change course and speed as the other vessel must keep clear Choice C: the other vessel must keep her course and speed Choice D: both vessels must keep their course and speed
response: Choice A: you must keep your course and speed

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel proceeding along a  narrow channel shall _____.
Choice A: avoid crossing the channel at right angles Choice B: not overtake any vessels within the channel Choice C: keep as near as safe and practicable to the limit of the channel on her starboard side Choice D: when nearing a bend in the channel, sound a long blast of the whistle
response: Choice C: keep as near as safe and practicable to the limit of the channel on her starboard side

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would exhibit  sidelights when underway and not making way?
Choice A: A vessel towing astern Choice B: A vessel trawling Choice C: A vessel not under command Choice D: A vessel engaged in dredging operations
response: Choice A: A vessel towing astern

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is NOT to impede the passage of a vessel which can only navigate safely  within a narrow channel?
Choice A: Any vessel less than 20 meters in length Choice B: Any sailing vessel Choice C: A vessel engaged in fishing Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A tug is towing three   manned barges in line in fog. The second vessel of the tow should sound ______________________.
Choice A: no fog signal Choice B: one short blast Choice C: one prolonged and three short blasts Choice D: one prolonged and two short blasts
response: Choice A: no fog signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The steering and sailing rules for vessels in restricted visibility apply to vessels _____.
Choice A: in sight of one another in fog Choice B: navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility Choice C: only if they are showing special purpose lights Choice D: only if they have operational radar
response: Choice B: navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Navigation Rules state that a vessel shall be operated at a safe speed at all times so that she can be stopped within _____.
Choice A: the distance of visibility Choice B: 1/2 the distance of visibility Choice C: a distance appropriate to the existing circumstances and conditions Choice D: the distance that it would require for the propeller to go from full ahead to full astern
response: Choice C: a distance appropriate to the existing circumstances and conditions

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel 35 meters in length, with a tow 100 meters astern, must show a minimum of how many masthead lights?
Choice A: 1 Choice B: 2 Choice C: 3 Choice D: 4
response: Choice B: 2

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What must be TRUE in order for a stand-on vessel to take action to avoid collision by her maneuver alone?
Choice A: She must be in sight of the give-way vessel. Choice B: There must be risk of collision. Choice C: She must determine that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel being towed astern, where the length of the tow exceeds 200 meters, will exhibit _________________.
Choice A: two balls in a vertical line Choice B: a diamond shape where it can best be seen Choice C: a ball on each end of the tow Choice D: no dayshape
response: Choice B: a diamond shape where it can best be seen

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND For a stand-on vessel to take action to avoid collision she shall, if possible, NOT  _______.
Choice A: decrease speed Choice B: increase speed Choice C: turn to port for a vessel on her port side Choice D: turn to starboard for a vessel on her port side
response: Choice C: turn to port for a vessel on her port side

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST __________.
Choice A: reduce speed to bare steerageway Choice B: stop your engines Choice C: begin a radar plot Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: reduce speed to bare steerageway

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Two barges are being pushed  ahead by a tugboat. Which statement is TRUE concerning  lights on the barges?
Choice A: Each vessel should show sidelights. Choice B: Each vessel should show at least one white light. Choice C: The barges should be lighted as separate units. Choice D: The barges should be lighted as one vessel.
response: Choice D: The barges should be lighted as one vessel.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Rules state that a seaplane shall _____________________.
Choice A: not be regarded as a vessel Choice B: in general, keep well clear of all vessels Choice C: proceed at a slower speed than surrounding vessels Choice D: when making way, show the lights for a vessel not under  command
response: Choice B: in general, keep well clear of all vessels

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If practical, when shall a  manned vessel being towed sound her fog signal?
Choice A: Immediately before the towing vessel sounds hers Choice B: Immediately after the towing vessel sounds hers Choice C: As close to the mid-cycle of the towing vessel's signals as possible Choice D: At any time as long as the interval is correct
response: Choice B: Immediately after the towing vessel sounds hers

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your tug is underway at night and NOT towing. What light(s) should your vessel show aft to other vessels coming up from astern?
Choice A: One white light Choice B: Two white lights Choice C: One white light and one yellow light Choice D: One white light and two yellow lights
response: Choice A: One white light

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel conducting mineclearing operations will show _________________.
Choice A: three balls in a vertical line Choice B: two balls in a vertical line Choice C: one ball near the foremast and one ball at each fore yard Choice D: one diamond near the foremast head and one ball at each  fore yard
response: Choice C: one ball near the foremast and one ball at each fore yard

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel sailing shall keep out of the way of all of the following vessels except a vessel ___________________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: engaged on pilotage duty Choice C: restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice D: engaged in fishing
response: Choice B: engaged on pilotage duty

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel under oars?
Choice A: She must show a sternlight. Choice B: She is allowed to show the same lights as a sailing vessel. Choice C: She must show a fixed all-round white light. Choice D: She must show a dayshape of a black cone.
response: Choice B: She is allowed to show the same lights as a sailing vessel.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel is  underway and fishing with trolling lines. This vessel  _____________________.
Choice A: must keep out of the way of sailing vessels Choice B: must sound a one prolonged, two short blasts signal in  restricted visibility Choice C: is the stand-on vessel when overtaking power-driven vessels Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: must keep out of the way of sailing vessels

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND At night you sight a vessel  displaying a single green light. This is a _____.
Choice A: vessel at anchor Choice B: small motorboat underway Choice C: vessel drifting Choice D: sailing vessel
response: Choice D: sailing vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When two power-driven vessels are crossing, which vessel is the stand-on vessel?
Choice A: The vessel which is to starboard of the other vessel Choice B: The vessel which is to port of the other vessel Choice C: The larger vessel Choice D: The vessel that sounds the first whistle signal
response: Choice A: The vessel which is to starboard of the other vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must exhibit forward and after white masthead lights when making way?
Choice A: A 75-meter vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice B: A 100-meter sailing vessel Choice C: A 150-meter vessel engaged in fishing Choice D: A 45-meter vessel engaged in towing
response: Choice A: A 75-meter vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND By radar alone, you detect a§vessel ahead on a collision course, about 3 miles distant.§ Your radar plot shows this to be a meeting situation. You§should _______.
Choice A: turn to port Choice B: turn to starboard Choice C: maintain course and speed and sound the danger signal Choice D: maintain course and speed and sound no signal
response: Choice B: turn to starboard

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel underway at night may show _________________.
Choice A: a red light over a green light at the masthead Choice B: a green light over a red light at the masthead Choice C: two white lights in a vertical line at the stern Choice D: an all-round white light at the bow
response: Choice A: a red light over a green light at the masthead

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in trawling will show identification lights of ___________________.
Choice A: a red light over a white light Choice B: a white light over a red light Choice C: a green light over a white light Choice D: two red lights in a vertical line
response: Choice C: a green light over a white light

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is required of a vessel§navigating near an area of restricted visibility?
Choice A: A power-driven vessel shall have her engines ready for  immediate maneuver. Choice B: She must sound appropriate sound signals. Choice C: If she detects another vessel by radar, she shall determine if risk of collision exists. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND By night, you sight the lights of a vessel engaged in underwater operations. If an   obstruction exists on the port side of the vessel, it will be marked by _________________.
Choice A: a floodlight Choice B: two red lights in a vertical line Choice C: a single red light Choice D: any visible lights
response: Choice B: two red lights in a vertical line

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may carry her  sidelights and sternlight in one combined lantern?
Choice A: A 10-meter power-driven vessel Choice B: A 15-meter vessel propelled by sail and machinery Choice C: A 10-meter sailing vessel Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: A 10-meter sailing vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which lights would be shown at night by a vessel which is restricted in her ability to  deviate from her course?
Choice A: Three red lights in a vertical line Choice B: Three white lights in a vertical line Choice C: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest  white and the middle red Choice D: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest red and the middle white
response: Choice D: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest red and the middle white

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel is the stand-on vessel when two vessels crossing in fog are NOT in sight of one another?
Choice A: The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side Choice B: The vessel which has the other on her own port side Choice C: The one which hears the other's fog signal first Choice D: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel.
response: Choice D: Neither vessel is the stand-on vessel.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  shall keep out of the way of a vessel _____.
Choice A: under sail Choice B: restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: crossing a channel Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: restricted in her ability to maneuver

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessels shall turn off their sidelights?
Choice A: All vessels that are not under command Choice B: All fishing vessels that are not making way Choice C: All sailing vessels which are becalmed Choice D: All vessels engaged in underwater operations
response: Choice B: All fishing vessels that are not making way

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel fishing at night, with gear extending more than 150 meters horizontally outwards, will show in the direction of the gear _________________.
Choice A: one white light Choice B: two vertical white lights Choice C: one yellow light Choice D: two vertical yellow lights
response: Choice A: one white light

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In restricted visibility, a  vessel which detects by radar alone the presence of another vessel shall determine if a close quarters situation is  developing or risk of collision exists. If so, she shall _____.
Choice A: sound the danger signal Choice B: when taking action, make only course changes Choice C: avoid altering course toward a vessel abaft the beam Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: avoid altering course toward a vessel abaft the beam

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 60-meter vessel which is  trawling is required to show how many white masthead lights at night?
Choice A: 1 Choice B: 2 Choice C: 3 Choice D: 4
response: Choice A: 1

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel servicing a pipeline during the day shall display ___________________.
Choice A: three black shapes in a vertical line; the highest and  lowest are balls, and the middle one is a diamond Choice B: three shapes in a vertical line; the highest and lowest are red balls, and the middle one is a white diamond Choice C: three black balls in a vertical line Choice D: two black balls in a vertical line
response: Choice A: three black shapes in a vertical line; the highest and  lowest are balls, and the middle one is a diamond

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In fog you observe your radar and determine that risk of collision exists with a vessel which is 2 miles off your port bow. You should __________.
Choice A: stop your engines Choice B: sound the danger signal at two-minute intervals Choice C: hold course and speed until the other vessel is sighted Choice D: take avoiding action as soon as possible
response: Choice D: take avoiding action as soon as possible

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a towing vessel which, due to the nature of her work, is unable to keep out of the way of another vessel?
Choice A: By day, she shall carry a black cylinder shape. Choice B: By day, she shall carry two black balls in a vertical line. Choice C: By night, she would show the same lights as a vessel not under command. Choice D: By day, she would show the same shapes as a vessel   restricted in her ability to maneuver.
response: Choice D: By day, she would show the same shapes as a vessel   restricted in her ability to maneuver.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   regarding equipment for bell & gong signals?
Choice A: A vessel of less than 12 meters in length need not have any sound signaling equipment. Choice B: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible. Choice C: Any vessel over 12 meters in length must be provided with a gong. Choice D: Signals must be able to be sounded manually and    automatically.
response: Choice B: Manual sounding of the signals must always be possible.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a narrow channel. You see a vessel that can only be navigated safely within the channel. You MUST _____.
Choice A: hold your course and speed Choice B: sound the danger signal Choice C: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel Choice D: initiate an exchange of passing signals
response: Choice C: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the minimum sound  signaling equipment required aboard a vessel 10 meters in length?
Choice A: Any means of making an efficient sound signal Choice B: A bell only Choice C: A whistle only Choice D: A bell and a whistle
response: Choice A: Any means of making an efficient sound signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel must have a gong, or other equipment which will make the sound of a gong?
Choice A: A sailing vessel Choice B: Any vessel over 50 meters Choice C: A power driven vessel over 75 meters Choice D: Any vessel over 100 meters
response: Choice D: Any vessel over 100 meters

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway and in sight of another vessel, less than one half mile away, you put your engines on astern propulsion. Which statement concerning whistle signals is TRUE?
Choice A: You need not sound any whistle signals. Choice B: You must sound one blast if backing to starboard. Choice C: You must sound whistle signals only if the vessels are  meeting. Choice D: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle.
response: Choice D: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE  concerning the light used with whistle signals?
Choice A: Use of such a light is required. Choice B: Its purpose is to supplement short blasts of the whistle. Choice C: The light shall have the same characteristics as a masthead light. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: Its purpose is to supplement short blasts of the whistle.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What determines if a vessel is "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Choice A: Whether or not all of the vessel's control equipment is in working order Choice B: The vessel's draft in relation to the available depth of water Choice C: Whether the nature of the vessel's work limits    maneuverability required by the Rules Choice D: Whether or not the vessel is the give-way vessel in a  meeting situation
response: Choice C: Whether the nature of the vessel's work limits    maneuverability required by the Rules

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is true   concerning the light used to accompany whistle signals?
Choice A: It is only used to supplement short blasts of the whistle. Choice B: It is mandatory to use such a light. Choice C: The light shall have the same characteristics as a masthead light. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: It is only used to supplement short blasts of the whistle.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is§TRUE concerning the danger signal?
Choice A: Only the stand-on vessel can sound the danger signal. Choice B: Radio transmissions may be used in place of the danger signal. Choice C: A vessel in doubt as to the other vessel's intentions must sound the danger signal. Choice D: The danger signal consists of 5 or more prolonged blasts of the whistle.
response: Choice C: A vessel in doubt as to the other vessel's intentions must sound the danger signal.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel may sound the  danger signal?
Choice A: Either vessel in a meeting situation Choice B: The give-way vessel in a crossing situation Choice C: A vessel at anchor Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are on watch in fog. Which vessel is "in sight"?
Choice A: A vessel that you can see from the bridge Choice B: A radar target of which you have determined the course and speed Choice C: A vessel from which you can hear the fog signal Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: A vessel that you can see from the bridge

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a meeting situation, which vessel may sound the danger signal?
Choice A: Stand-on vessel Choice B: Give-way vessel Choice C: Either vessel Choice D: Neither vessel
response: Choice C: Either vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are underway in a narrow channel and are being overtaken by a vessel astern. The overtaking vessel sounds a signal indicating her intention to pass you on your starboard side. If such an action  appears dangerous, you should sound ______________.
Choice A: one prolonged followed by one short blast Choice B: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast in that order Choice C: five short and rapid blasts Choice D: three short and rapid blasts
response: Choice C: five short and rapid blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which is a light signal   authorized by the Secretary of the Navy as an additional navigational light for a ship of war?
Choice A: Flashing amber beacon for submarines Choice B: Green masthead and yardarm lights indicating mine clearance operations Choice C: Red-white-red lights in a vertical line for a carrier,  launching aircraft Choice D: Yellow flares indicating torpedo firing exercises
response: Choice A: Flashing amber beacon for submarines

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Dayshapes must be displayed _____.
Choice A: between sunset and sunrise Choice B: only between 8 AM and 4 PM Choice C: during daylight hours in any visibility Choice D: during daylight hours in unrestricted visibility only
response: Choice C: during daylight hours in any visibility

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel may exhibit lights §other than those prescribed by the Rules as long as the §additional lights _____.
Choice A: are not the same color as either side light Choice B: have a lesser range of visibility than the prescribed lights Choice C: do not impair the visibility or distinctive character of the prescribed lights Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: do not impair the visibility or distinctive character of the prescribed lights

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel may exhibit lights  other than those prescribed by the Rules as long as the  additional lights _____.
Choice A: do not interfere with the keeping of a proper look-out Choice B: do not impair the visibility or distinctive character of the prescribed lights Choice C: cannot be mistaken for the lights specified elsewhere in the Rules Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The sternlight shall be   positioned such that it will show from dead astern to how many degrees on each side of the stern of the vessel?
Choice A: 135.0° Choice B: 112.5° Choice C: 67.5° Choice D: 22.5°
response: Choice C: 67.5°

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see a red sidelight bearing NW (315°). That vessel may be heading _________.
Choice A: northwest (315°) Choice B: east (090°) Choice C: southwest (225°) Choice D: west (270°)
response: Choice C: southwest (225°)

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What does the word "breadth" mean?
Choice A: Greatest breadth Choice B: Molded breadth Choice C: Breadth on the main deck Choice D: Breadth at the load waterline
response: Choice A: Greatest breadth

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If underway in low visibility and sounding fog signals, what changes would you make in the fog signal IMMEDIATELY upon losing the power plant and propulsion?
Choice A: Begin sounding one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at two-minute intervals. Choice B: Begin sounding one prolonged blast followed by three short blasts at two-minute intervals. Choice C: Begin sounding two prolonged blasts at two-minute intervals. Choice D: No change should be made in the fog signal.
response: Choice A: Begin sounding one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at two-minute intervals.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  while at anchor shall sound a fog signal of ______________.
Choice A: one prolonged and three short blasts at one minute   intervals Choice B: a rapid ringing of the bell for five seconds at one minute intervals Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts at two minute intervals Choice D: a sounding of the bell and gong at one minute intervals
response: Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts at two minute intervals

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is the fog signal for a vessel 75 meters in length, restricted in her ability to maneuver, at anchor?
Choice A: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at   intervals of not more than two minutes Choice B: Five second ringing of a bell at intervals of not more than one minute Choice C: Four short blasts at intervals of not more than two minutes Choice D: Five second ringing of a bell and five second sounding of a gong at intervals of not more than one minute
response: Choice A: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at   intervals of not more than two minutes

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel sounds the same fog signal when underway or at anchor?
Choice A: A sailing vessel Choice B: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice C: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice D: A vessel not under command
response: Choice C: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which vessel would sound a fog signal consisting of the ringing of a bell for 5 seconds?
Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing, at anchor Choice B: A vessel restricted in its ability to maneuver, at anchor Choice C: A sailing vessel, at anchor Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: A sailing vessel, at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 200-meter vessel is aground in fog. Which signal is optional?
Choice A: A bell signal Choice B: A whistle signal Choice C: A gong signal Choice D: All of the above are mandatory.
response: Choice B: A whistle signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What is NOT a vessel "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Choice A: A vessel laying engaged in laying submarine cable Choice B: A vessel towing with limited maneuverability due to a large unwieldy tow Choice C: A deep-draft vessel that can only navigate in a dredged  channel Choice D: A towing vessel underway with a fuel barge alongside and taking on fuel
response: Choice C: A deep-draft vessel that can only navigate in a dredged  channel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A 200-meter vessel is aground in restricted visibility. Which signal is optional?
Choice A: A whistle signal Choice B: A gong signal Choice C: A bell signal Choice D: All of the above are optional.
response: Choice A: A whistle signal

instruction:
