instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Power-driven vessels must keep out of the way of sailing vessels except ___________.
Choice A: in a crossing situation Choice B: when they are making more speed than the power-driven  vessel Choice C: when the sailing vessel is overtaking Choice D: on the Inland Waters of the United States
response: Choice C: when the sailing vessel is overtaking

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND When do the Rules require both vessels to change course?
Choice A: Any time the danger signal is sounded Choice B: When two power-driven vessels are crossing and it is  apparent to the stand-on vessel that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action Choice C: When two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: When two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Your vessel is NOT making way, but is not in any way disabled. Another vessel is   approaching you on your starboard beam. Which statement is TRUE?
Choice A: Your vessel is obligated to stay out of the way. Choice B: The other vessel must give way, since your vessel is  stopped. Choice C: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel not under command. Choice D: You should be showing the lights or shapes for a vessel  restricted in her ability to maneuver.
response: Choice A: Your vessel is obligated to stay out of the way.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If you are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation, you may take action to avoid  collision by your maneuver alone. When may this action be taken?
Choice A: As soon as you determine that risk of collision exists Choice B: Only when you have reached extremis Choice C: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action Choice D: When you determine that your present course will cross ahead of the other vessel
response: Choice C: When it becomes apparent to you that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a crossing situation on§open waters, a sailing vessel shall keep out of the way of§all the following vessels EXCEPT a vessel _____.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: engaged in towing Choice D: fishing
response: Choice C: engaged in towing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What would be a "special  circumstance" under the Rules?
Choice A: Vessel at anchor Choice B: Two vessels meeting Choice C: Speed in fog Choice D: More than two vessels crossing
response: Choice D: More than two vessels crossing

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In restricted visibility, a  vessel being towed, if manned, shall sound a signal of ____.
Choice A: one prolonged and three short blasts Choice B: one prolonged and two short blasts Choice C: three short blasts Choice D: two short blasts
response: Choice A: one prolonged and three short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are approaching a narrow§channel. Another vessel in the channel can only be§navigated safely in that channel. You should _____________.
Choice A: sound two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast Choice B: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel Choice C: sound three short blasts, and take all way off your vessel Choice D: hold your course and speed if he is on your port bow
response: Choice B: not cross the channel if you might impede the other vessel

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You are the stand-on vessel in a crossing situation. If you think the give-way vessel is NOT taking sufficient action to avoid collision, you should sound _____________________.
Choice A: one short blast and maintain course Choice B: two short blasts, alter to port, and pass astern Choice C: the danger signal Choice D: no signal and maneuver at will
response: Choice C: the danger signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel ahead sound two prolonged blasts on the whistle. You should _____.
Choice A: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted Choice B: not sound any whistle signals until the other vessel is  sighted Choice C: sound two blasts and change course to the left Choice D: sound whistle signals only if you change course
response: Choice A: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Lighting requirements in§inland waters are different from those for international§waters for _____.
Choice A: barges being towed astern Choice B: vessels not under command Choice C: vessels pushing ahead Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: vessels pushing ahead

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND There are two classes of vessels which do not have to comply with the rule regarding traffic separation schemes, to the extent necessary to carry out their work. One of those is a vessel _______________.
Choice A: engaged in fishing Choice B: towing another Choice C: servicing a navigational aid Choice D: on pilotage duty
response: Choice C: servicing a navigational aid

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a traffic separation scheme, when joining a traffic lane from the side, a vessel shall do so _____________.
Choice A: only in case of an emergency or to engage in fishing within the zone Choice B: as nearly as practical at right angles to the general  direction of traffic flow Choice C: at as small an angle as possible Choice D: only to anchor within the zone
response: Choice C: at as small an angle as possible

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A traffic separation zone is that part of a traffic separation scheme which __________.
Choice A: is located between the scheme and the nearest land Choice B: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction Choice C: is designated as an anchorage area Choice D: contains all the traffic moving in the same direction
response: Choice B: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall _______________.
Choice A: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme Choice B: avoid crossing traffic lanes, but if obliged to do so, shall cross on as small an angle as is practical Choice C: only anchor in the separation zone Choice D: use the separation zone for navigating through the scheme if she is hindering other traffic due to her slower speed
response: Choice A: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall NOT _____________.
Choice A: cross a traffic lane Choice B: engage in fishing the separation zone Choice C: proceed in an inappropriate traffic lane Choice D: enter the separation zone
response: Choice C: proceed in an inappropriate traffic lane

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme shall _____.
Choice A: only anchor in the separation zone Choice B: avoid crossing traffic lanes, but if obliged to do so, shall cross on a heading at as small an angle as is practical Choice C: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme Choice D: use the separation zone for navigation through the scheme if she is hindering other traffic due to her slower speed
response: Choice C: avoid anchoring in areas near the termination of the scheme

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel ahead sound two prolonged blasts on the whistle. You should _______________________.
Choice A: sound two blasts and change course to the left Choice B: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted Choice C: sound whistle signals only if you change course Choice D: not sound any whistle signals until the other vessel is  sighted
response: Choice B: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing vessel and her tow are severely restricted in their ability to change course. §When making way, the towing vessel will show ONLY _____.
Choice A: the masthead lights for a towing vessel Choice B: the lights for a vessel restricted in her ability to  maneuver Choice C: sidelights,stern light, and towing light Choice D: All of the above.
response: Choice D: All of the above.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST __________.
Choice A: take all way off, if necessary Choice B: stop your engines Choice C: begin a radar plot Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice A: take all way off, if necessary

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fog signal of one short, one prolonged, and one short blast may be sounded by a _____.
Choice A: vessel not under command Choice B: vessel at anchor Choice C: vessel towing Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: vessel at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You hear the fog signal of  another vessel forward of your beam. Risk of collision may exist. You MUST _____.
Choice A: stop your engines Choice B: take all way off, if necessary Choice C: begin a radar plot Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: take all way off, if necessary

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel may enter a traffic separation zone ___________.
Choice A: in an emergency Choice B: to engage in fishing within the zone Choice C: to cross the traffic separation scheme Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND In a traffic separation scheme, when joining a traffic lane from the side, a vessel shall do so _______________.
Choice A: at as small an angle as possible Choice B: as nearly as practical at right angles to the general  direction of traffic flow Choice C: only in case of an emergency or to engage in fishing within the zone Choice D: never
response: Choice A: at as small an angle as possible

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel using a traffic  separation scheme is forbidden to _________________.
Choice A: proceed through an inappropriate traffic lane Choice B: engaged in fishing in the separation zone Choice C: cross a traffic lane Choice D: enter the separation zone, even in a emergency
response: Choice A: proceed through an inappropriate traffic lane

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A traffic separation zone is that part of a traffic separation scheme which ________.
Choice A: is between the scheme and the nearest land Choice B: contains all the traffic moving in one direction Choice C: is designated as an anchorage area Choice D: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction
response: Choice D: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY To indicate that a vessel is constrained by her draft, a vessel may display, in a vertical line,  ____________.
Choice A: three 360° red lights Choice B: two 225° red lights Choice C: three 360° blue lights Choice D: two 225° blue lights
response: Choice A: three 360° red lights

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A power-driven vessel pushing ahead§or towing alongside displays navigation lights and _____.
Choice A: two all-round red lights in a vertical line Choice B: two yellow towing lights in a vertical line Choice C: two white masthead lights in a vertical line Choice D: two lights on the stern, one yellow and one white
response: Choice C: two white masthead lights in a vertical line

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is true concerning a  vessel "constrained by her draft"?
Choice A: She must be a power-driven vessel. Choice B: She is not under command. Choice C: She may be a vessel being towed. Choice D: She is hampered because of her work.
response: Choice A: She must be a power-driven vessel.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY When moving from a berth alongside a quay (wharf), a vessel must sound _____.
Choice A: three short blasts Choice B: a long blast Choice C: a prolonged blast Choice D: No signal is required.
response: Choice D: No signal is required.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are in charge of a 250-meter freight vessel constrained by her draft proceeding down a narrow channel. There is a vessel engaged in fishing on your starboard bow half a mile away. §According to Rule 9, which statement is TRUE?
Choice A: You are not to impede the fishing vessel. Choice B: If you are in doubt as to the fishing vessel's intentions you may sound at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle. Choice C: You are to slow to bare steerageway until clear of the  fishing vessel. Choice D: You must sound one prolonged blast to alert the fishing vessel.
response: Choice B: If you are in doubt as to the fishing vessel's intentions you may sound at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY The International Rules of the Road apply _______________________.
Choice A: to all waters which are not inland waters Choice B: only to waters outside the territorial waters of the United States Choice C: only to waters where foreign vessels travel Choice D: upon the high seas and connecting waters navigable by  seagoing vessels
response: Choice D: upon the high seas and connecting waters navigable by  seagoing vessels

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A towing light is _____.
Choice A: shown at the bow Choice B: white in color Choice C: shown in addition to the sternlight Choice D: an all-round light
response: Choice C: shown in addition to the sternlight

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, an overtaking vessel which intends to pass on the other vessel's port side would sound _____.
Choice A: one prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice B: one short blast Choice C: two short blasts Choice D: two prolonged followed by two short blasts
response: Choice D: two prolonged followed by two short blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are underway on the high seas in  restricted visibility. You hear a fog signal of one  prolonged and two short blasts. It could be any of the  following EXCEPT a vessel _____.
Choice A: minesweeping Choice B: engaged in fishing Choice C: constrained by her draft Choice D: being towed
response: Choice D: being towed

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel displaying three red lights in a vertical line is ___________________.
Choice A: not under command Choice B: aground Choice C: dredging Choice D: constrained by her draft
response: Choice D: constrained by her draft

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY At night, a power-driven vessel underway of less than 7 meters in length where its maximum speed does not exceed 7 knots may show, as a minimum, _____.
Choice A: sidelights and a sternlight Choice B: the lights required for a vessel more than 7 meters in  length Choice C: sidelights only Choice D: one all-round white light
response: Choice D: one all-round white light

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, a signal of intent which must be answered by the other vessel, is sounded by a vessel ____________________.
Choice A: meeting another head-on Choice B: crossing the course of another Choice C: overtaking another Choice D: Any of the above
response: Choice C: overtaking another

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY When two vessels are in sight of one  another, all of the following signals may be given EXCEPT _____________________.
Choice A: a light signal of at least five short and rapid flashes Choice B: four short whistle blasts Choice C: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged and one short  whistle blasts Choice D: two short whistle blasts
response: Choice B: four short whistle blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A power-driven vessel leaving a quay or wharf must sound what signal?
Choice A: Three short blasts Choice B: A long blast Choice C: A prolonged blast Choice D: No signal is required.
response: Choice D: No signal is required.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Lighting requirements in inland waters are different from those in international waters for _____.
Choice A: barges being pushed ahead Choice B: vessels constrained by their draft Choice C: vessels towing by pushing ahead Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY What whistle signal, if any, would be sounded when two vessels are meeting, but will pass clear starboard to starboard?
Choice A: One short blast Choice B: Two short blasts Choice C: Five or more short blasts Choice D: No signal is required.
response: Choice D: No signal is required.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, a vessel trying to overtake another on the other vessel's port side, would  sound a whistle signal of _________________.
Choice A: one short blast Choice B: two short blasts Choice C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast Choice D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
response: Choice D: two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY On open water, a power-driven vessel  coming up dead astern of another vessel and altering her course to starboard so as to pass on the starboard side of the vessel ahead would sound _____________.
Choice A: two short blasts Choice B: one short blast Choice C: two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast Choice D: one long and one short blast
response: Choice B: one short blast

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY If a vessel displays three all-round red lights in a vertical line at night, during the day she may show ___________.
Choice A: three balls in a vertical line Choice B: a cylinder Choice C: two diamonds in a vertical line Choice D: two cones, apexes together
response: Choice B: a cylinder

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel not under command sounds the same fog signal as a vessel _____.
Choice A: towing Choice B: constrained by her draft Choice C: under sail Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Your vessel is crossing a narrow channel. A vessel to port is within the channel and crossing your course. She is showing a black cylinder. What is your  responsibility?
Choice A: Hold your course and speed. Choice B: Sound the danger signal. Choice C: Begin an exchange of passing signals. Choice D: Do not cross the channel if you might impede the other  vessel.
response: Choice D: Do not cross the channel if you might impede the other  vessel.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are approaching another vessel and will pass starboard to starboard without danger if no course changes are made. You should ___________________.
Choice A: hold course and sound a two blast whistle signal Choice B: hold course and sound no whistle signal Choice C: change course to the right and sound one blast Choice D: hold course and sound two prolonged and two short blasts
response: Choice B: hold course and sound no whistle signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A fishing vessel is approaching a vessel not under command. Which statement is TRUE?
Choice A: The fishing vessel must keep clear of the vessel not under command. Choice B: If the vessel not under command is a power-driven vessel, she must keep clear of the fishing vessel. Choice C: They must exchange whistle signals. Choice D: Both vessels are required to take action to stay clear of each other.
response: Choice A: The fishing vessel must keep clear of the vessel not under command.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which signal is required to be sounded by a power driven vessel ONLY?
Choice A: A signal meaning, "I am altering my course to starboard." Choice B: A signal meaning, "I intend to overtake you on your starboard side." Choice C: A signal meaning that the vessel sounding it is in doubt as to the other vessel's actions. Choice D: A signal sounded when approaching a bend.
response: Choice A: A signal meaning, "I am altering my course to starboard."

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY The light which may be used with a  vessel's whistle is to be ___________________.
Choice A: used when the whistle is broken Choice B: used prior to sounding the whistle Choice C: used only at night Choice D: a white light
response: Choice D: a white light

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are in sight of another vessel in a crossing situation, and the other vessel sounds one short blast. You are going to hold course and speed. You should _______________________.
Choice A: answer with one short blast Choice B: answer with two short blasts Choice C: sound the danger signal Choice D: sound no whistle signal
response: Choice D: sound no whistle signal

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Two prolonged blasts followed by one  short blast on the whistle is a signal which could be  sounded by a _________________.
Choice A: fishing vessel Choice B: vessel anchored Choice C: mineclearing vessel Choice D: vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel
response: Choice D: vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a crossing situation on international waters, a short blast by the give-way vessel indicates that the vessel ________.
Choice A: is holding course and speed Choice B: is turning to starboard Choice C: intends to pass port to port Choice D: will keep out of the way of the stand-on vessel
response: Choice B: is turning to starboard

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY What dayshape is prescribed for a vessel constrained by her draft?
Choice A: A black cone, apex upward Choice B: A black cone, apex downward Choice C: Two vertical black balls Choice D: A cylinder
response: Choice D: A cylinder

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel not under command sounds the same fog signal as a vessel _____________________.
Choice A: engaged in towing Choice B: constrained by her draft Choice C: under sail Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement(s) is(are) TRUE concerning light signals?
Choice A: The time between flashes shall be about five seconds. Choice B: The time between successive signals shall be not less than ten seconds. Choice C: The light signals are to be used when not using sound  signals. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: The time between successive signals shall be not less than ten seconds.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Under what circumstances would an  overtaking vessel sound a whistle signal of two prolonged followed by one short blast?
Choice A: When overtaking in restricted visibility Choice B: When overtaking in a narrow channel Choice C: When overtaking on open waters Choice D: When no other vessels are in the immediate area
response: Choice B: When overtaking in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In which case would an overtaking vessel sound a whistle signal of two prolonged followed by one  short blast?
Choice A: When overtaking in restricted visibility Choice B: When overtaking in a narrow channel Choice C: When overtaking on open waters Choice D: When no other vessels are in the immediate area
response: Choice B: When overtaking in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY When vessels are in sight of one another, two short blasts from one of the vessels means ____________.
Choice A: "I am altering my course to starboard" Choice B: "I am altering my course to port" Choice C: "I intend to change course to starboard" Choice D: "I intend to change course to port"
response: Choice B: "I am altering my course to port"

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel may NOT exhibit two red  lights in a vertical line?
Choice A: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice B: A trawler fishing in close proximity to other trawlers Choice C: A vessel aground Choice D: A dredge
response: Choice A: A vessel constrained by her draft

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Vessel "A" is overtaking vessel "B" on open waters and will pass without changing course. Vessel "A" ___________.
Choice A: should sound two short blasts Choice B: should sound the danger signal Choice C: should sound one long blast Choice D: will not sound any whistle signals
response: Choice D: will not sound any whistle signals

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Of the vessels listed, which must keep out of the way of all the others?
Choice A: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice B: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: A vessel on pilotage duty Choice D: A vessel engaged in fishing
response: Choice C: A vessel on pilotage duty

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel would NOT sound a fog signal of one prolonged and two short blasts?
Choice A: A vessel not under command Choice B: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice C: A vessel being towed Choice D: A vessel sailing
response: Choice C: A vessel being towed

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In international waters, you are on  Vessel "I" in the situation shown in DIAGRAM 36. Vessel "II" sounds one short blast. Which action should you take?
Choice A: Sound one short blast and hold course and speed. Choice B: Hold course and speed Choice C: Sound one short blast and slow down or turn to starboard. Choice D: Sound two short blasts, slow down and turn to port
response: Choice B: Hold course and speed

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You intend to overtake a vessel in a  narrow channel, and you intend to pass along the vessel's port side. How should you signal your intention?
Choice A: No signal is necessary. Choice B: Two prolonged blasts Choice C: Two short blasts Choice D: Two prolonged followed by two short blasts
response: Choice D: Two prolonged followed by two short blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel sounds two short blasts. This signal indicates the vessel ___________________.
Choice A: intends to alter course to port Choice B: intends to pass starboard to starboard Choice C: is altering course to port Choice D: will alter course to port
response: Choice C: is altering course to port

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel sounds one short blast. This signal indicates the vessel _________________.
Choice A: intends to alter course to starboard Choice B: intends to pass starboard to starboard Choice C: is altering course to starboard Choice D: intends to pass port to port
response: Choice C: is altering course to starboard

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are underway in a narrow channel, and you are being overtaken by a vessel astern. After the  overtaking vessel sounds the proper signal indicating his intention to pass your vessel on your starboard side, you signal your agreement by sounding ___________.
Choice A: one short blast Choice B: two prolonged blasts Choice C: two prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice D: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast in that order
response: Choice D: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast in that order

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which signal is sounded ONLY when§vessels are NOT in sight of each other?
Choice A: A signal of at least five short and rapid blasts Choice B: Four short blasts on the whistle Choice C: One prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast on the whistle, in that order Choice D: Two short blasts on the whistle
response: Choice B: Four short blasts on the whistle

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A sailing vessel is overtaking a   power-driven vessel in a narrow channel, so as to pass on the power-driven vessel's port side. The overtaken vessel will have to move to facilitate passage. The sailing vessel is the ___________________.
Choice A: stand-on vessel and would sound two short blasts Choice B: give-way vessel and would sound no whistle signal Choice C: stand-on vessel and would sound no whistle signal Choice D: give-way vessel and would sound two prolonged blasts  followed by two short blasts
response: Choice D: give-way vessel and would sound two prolonged blasts  followed by two short blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel constrained by her draft may display _______________.
Choice A: three all-round red lights Choice B: two 225° red lights Choice C: three all-round blue lights Choice D: two 225° blue lights
response: Choice A: three all-round red lights

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Two power-driven vessels are meeting. A two blast whistle signal by either vessel means __________.
Choice A: "I intend to alter course to port" Choice B: "I desire to pass starboard to starboard" Choice C: "I desire to pass port to port" Choice D: "I am altering course to port"
response: Choice D: "I am altering course to port"

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A 20-meter power-driven vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside will display _____.
Choice A: a single white light forward Choice B: two masthead lights in a vertical line Choice C: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice D: two all-round red lights where they can best be seen
response: Choice B: two masthead lights in a vertical line

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement applies to a vessel  "constrained by her draft"?
Choice A: She is severely restricted in her ability to change her  course because of her draft in relation to the available depth of water. Choice B: The term applies only to vessels in marked channels. Choice C: She is designated as a "vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver". Choice D: The vessel must be over 100 meters in length.
response: Choice A: She is severely restricted in her ability to change her  course because of her draft in relation to the available depth of water.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A whistle signal of one prolonged, one short, one prolonged and one short blast, is sounded by a vessel ___________.
Choice A: at anchor Choice B: towing a submerged object Choice C: being overtaken in a narrow channel Choice D: in distress
response: Choice C: being overtaken in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Your vessel is backing out of a slip in a harbor and you can see that other vessels are approaching. You should sound _____.
Choice A: three short blasts when leaving the slip Choice B: one prolonged blast followed by three short blasts when the last line is taken aboard Choice C: one prolonged blast only Choice D: the danger signal
response: Choice A: three short blasts when leaving the slip

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel is to keep out of the way of the others?
Choice A: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice B: A vessel engaged in underwater operations Choice C: A vessel engaged in trawling Choice D: A vessel not under command
response: Choice C: A vessel engaged in trawling

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are in sight of a power-driven vessel that sounds two short blasts of the whistle. This signal means that the vessel ___________________.
Choice A: is altering course to port Choice B: is altering course to starboard Choice C: intends to leave you on her port side Choice D: intends to leave you on her starboard side
response: Choice A: is altering course to port

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are operating a vessel in a§narrow channel. Your vessel must stay within the channel to§be navigated safely. Another vessel is crossing your§course from starboard to port, and you are in doubt as to§his intentions. According to Rule 9, you ______.
Choice A: may sound the danger signal Choice B: must sound one prolonged and two short blasts Choice C: should sound one short blast to indicate that you are holding course and speed Choice D: are required to back down
response: Choice A: may sound the danger signal

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY If you sighted three red lights in a  vertical line on another vessel at night, it would be a  vessel _________________.
Choice A: aground Choice B: constrained by her draft Choice C: dredging Choice D: moored over a wreck
response: Choice B: constrained by her draft

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY On open water two vessels are in an  overtaking situation. The overtaking vessel has just  sounded one short blast on the whistle. What is the meaning of this whistle signal?
Choice A: "I request permission to pass you on my port side." Choice B: "I will maintain course and speed and pass you on your  starboard side." Choice C: "On which side should I pass?" Choice D: "I am changing course to starboard."
response: Choice D: "I am changing course to starboard."

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are underway in fog and hear a fog signal consisting of one prolonged and two short blasts. It could be any of the following EXCEPT a vessel _____________.
Choice A: engaged in mineclearance Choice B: engaged in fishing Choice C: constrained by her draft Choice D: being towed
response: Choice D: being towed

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel shall avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft?
Choice A: A vessel not under command Choice B: A fishing vessel Choice C: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: A fishing vessel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A signal of one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast, in that order is given by a vessel _________.
Choice A: engaged on pilotage duty Choice B: in distress Choice C: at anchor Choice D: being overtaken in a narrow channel
response: Choice D: being overtaken in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which signal is sounded ONLY by a§vessel in sight of another and NOT in or near an area§of restricted visibility?
Choice A: Four short blasts on the whistle Choice B: One prolonged blast on the whistle Choice C: One short blast on the whistle Choice D: One short, one prolonged, and one short blast on the whistle
response: Choice C: One short blast on the whistle

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In addition to her running lights, an underway vessel constrained by her draft may carry in a  vertical line _______________.
Choice A: a red light, a white light, and a red light Choice B: two red lights Choice C: two white lights Choice D: three red lights
response: Choice D: three red lights

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel is NOT regarded as being "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Choice A: A vessel servicing an aid to navigation Choice B: A vessel engaged in dredging Choice C: A towing vessel with tow unable to deviate from its course Choice D: A vessel constrained by her draft
response: Choice D: A vessel constrained by her draft

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY When two vessels are in sight of one§another and NOT in or near an area of restricted visibility,§any of the following signals may be given EXCEPT _________.
Choice A: a light signal of at least five short and rapid flashes Choice B: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short whistle blasts Choice C: four short whistle blasts Choice D: two short whistle blasts
response: Choice C: four short whistle blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY In a narrow channel, an overtaking vessel which intends to PASS on the other vessel's port side would sound _______________.
Choice A: one prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice B: one short blast Choice C: two prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice D: two short blasts
response: Choice C: two prolonged followed by two short blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Two prolonged blasts followed by one  short blast on the whistle is a signal which would be  sounded by a vessel __________________.
Choice A: overtaking another in a narrow channel Choice B: anchored Choice C: engaged in mineclearance Choice D: engaged in fishing
response: Choice A: overtaking another in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You intend to overtake a vessel in a  narrow channel, and you intend to pass along the vessel's port side. How should you signal your intention?
Choice A: Two short blasts followed by two prolonged blasts Choice B: Two prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice C: Two prolonged blasts only Choice D: Two short blasts only
response: Choice B: Two prolonged followed by two short blasts

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are underway in a narrow channel, and you are being overtaken by a vessel astern. After the  overtaking vessel sounds the proper signal indicating his intention to pass your vessel on your starboard side, you signal your agreement by sounding __________.
Choice A: two prolonged followed by two short blasts Choice B: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast Choice C: one short blast Choice D: two prolonged blasts
response: Choice B: one prolonged, one short, one prolonged, and one short blast

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Vessel "A" is overtaking vessel "B"§on open waters and will pass without changing course. §Vessel "A" should _________________.
Choice A: sound two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts Choice B: sound the danger signal Choice C: not sound any whistle signals Choice D: sound one long blast
response: Choice C: not sound any whistle signals

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which signal is sounded ONLY by a§vessel in sight of another?
Choice A: One short blast on the whistle Choice B: Four short blasts on the whistle Choice C: One prolonged blast on the whistle Choice D: One short, one prolonged, and one short blast on the whistle
response: Choice A: One short blast on the whistle

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY The light which may be used with a  vessel's whistle must be _________________.
Choice A: used when the whistle is broken Choice B: a white light Choice C: used only at night Choice D: used prior to sounding the whistle
response: Choice B: a white light

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning light signals?
Choice A: The time between flashes shall be about five seconds. Choice B: The light signals are to be used when not using sound  signals. Choice C: The time between successive signals shall be not less than ten seconds. Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice C: The time between successive signals shall be not less than ten seconds.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY While underway and in sight of§another vessel, you put your engines full speed astern. §Which statement concerning whistle signals is TRUE?
Choice A: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle. Choice B: You must sound one blast if backing to starboard. Choice C: You must sound whistle signals only if the vessels are meeting. Choice D: You need not sound any whistle signals.
response: Choice A: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY At night, a power-driven vessel less than 7 meters in length, with a maximum speed which does not  exceed 7 knots, may show when underway _____.
Choice A: sidelights combined in a single lantern Choice B: an all-round flashing yellow light Choice C: one all-round white light Choice D: a lantern showing a white light exhibited in sufficient time to prevent collision
response: Choice C: one all-round white light

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY At night, a power-driven vessel less than 7 meters in length, with a maximum speed which does not  exceed 7 knots, MUST show when underway at least _____.
Choice A: one white 360° light Choice B: a white light on the near approach of another vessel Choice C: sidelights and a sternlight Choice D: the lights required of a vessel less than 12 meters in  length
response: Choice A: one white 360° light

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Lighting requirements in inland waters are different from those for international waters for _____.
Choice A: barges being towed by pushing ahead Choice B: vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver Choice C: vessels towing astern Choice D: barges being towed astern
response: Choice A: barges being towed by pushing ahead

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A 20-meter power-driven vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside will display _____.
Choice A: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice B: a towing light above the sternlight Choice C: two all-round red lights at the masthead Choice D: two masthead lights in a vertical line
response: Choice D: two masthead lights in a vertical line

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A towing light _____.
Choice A: flashes at regular intervals of 50-70 flashes per minute Choice B: is yellow in color Choice C: shows an unbroken light over an arc of the horizon of not less than 180° nor more than 225° Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: is yellow in color

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A towing light is ____________ .
Choice A: shown below the sternlight Choice B: white in color Choice C: displayed at the masthead Choice D: a yellow light having the same characteristics as the stern light
response: Choice D: a yellow light having the same characteristics as the stern light

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be an ________________________.
Choice A: alternating red and yellow light Choice B: alternating white and yellow light Choice C: all-round white or yellow light Choice D: all-round white light only
response: Choice D: all-round white light only

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel constrained by her draft may display ___________________.
Choice A: three all-round red lights instead of the lights required for a power-driven vessel of her class Choice B: the same lights as a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: three all-round red lights in addition to the lights  required for a power-driven vessel of her class Choice D: the lights for a power-driven vessel which is not under  command
response: Choice C: three all-round red lights in addition to the lights  required for a power-driven vessel of her class

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which dayshape is prescribed for a vessel constrained by her draft?
Choice A: A black diamond Choice B: A cylinder Choice C: A black ball Choice D: A black cone, apex upward
response: Choice B: A cylinder

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY If at night a vessel displays three  all-round red lights in a vertical line, during the day she may show ___________.
Choice A: two cones, base to base Choice B: three black balls in a vertical line Choice C: a cylinder Choice D: a cone, apex downward
response: Choice C: a cylinder

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A vessel displaying three red lights in a vertical line is _____________________________________.
Choice A: restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice B: not under command Choice C: engaged in mineclearing operations Choice D: constrained by her draft
response: Choice D: constrained by her draft

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY The International Rules of the Road  apply _________.
Choice A: to all waters Choice B: to any waters inside the territorial waters of the U.S. Choice C: only to waters where foreign vessels travel Choice D: upon the high seas and connecting waters navigable by  seagoing vessels
response: Choice D: upon the high seas and connecting waters navigable by  seagoing vessels

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement applies to a vessel  "constrained by her draft"?
Choice A: The term only applies to vessels in narrow channels. Choice B: She is severely restricted in her ability to change her  course because of her draft in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water. Choice C: She is designated as a "vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver". Choice D: The vessel must be over 100 meters in length.
response: Choice B: She is severely restricted in her ability to change her  course because of her draft in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning a vessel "constrained by her draft"?
Choice A: She is hampered because of her work. Choice B: She is unable to maneuver due to some exceptional   circumstance. Choice C: She may be a vessel being towed. Choice D: She must be a power-driven vessel.
response: Choice D: She must be a power-driven vessel.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel is NOT "restricted in her ability to maneuver"?
Choice A: A vessel servicing an aid to navigation Choice B: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice C: A towing vessel with tow, unable to deviate from its course Choice D: A vessel engaged in dredging
response: Choice B: A vessel constrained by her draft

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Your vessel is constrained by her§draft and operating in a narrow channel. Another vessel§is crossing your course from starboard to port. You are§in doubt as to her intentions. According to Rule 9, you ________________.
Choice A: should sound one short blast to indicate that you are holding course and speed Choice B: must sound one prolonged blast Choice C: may sound the danger signal Choice D: are required to back down
response: Choice C: may sound the danger signal

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Your vessel is crossing a narrow channel. A vessel to port is within the channel and crossing your course. She is showing a black cylinder. You should _____.
Choice A: hold your course and speed Choice B: not impede the other vessel Choice C: exchange passing signals Choice D: sound the danger signal
response: Choice B: not impede the other vessel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Your vessel is backing out of a slip in a harbor. Visibility is restricted. You should sound  ____________________.
Choice A: one prolonged blast only Choice B: one prolonged blast followed by three short blasts when the last line is taken aboard Choice C: one prolonged blast followed by three short blasts when  leaving the slip Choice D: the danger signal
response: Choice A: one prolonged blast only

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are approaching another vessel and will pass safely starboard to starboard without changing course. You should _____.
Choice A: hold course and sound no whistle signal Choice B: hold course and sound a two blast whistle signal Choice C: change course to starboard and sound one blast Choice D: hold course and sound one blast
response: Choice A: hold course and sound no whistle signal

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL AND INLAND Which statement is TRUE concerning a situation involving a fishing vessel and a vessel not under command?
Choice A: They are required to communicate by radiotelephone. Choice B: If the vessel not under command is a power-driven vessel, she must keep clear of the fishing vessel. Choice C: The fishing vessel must keep out of the way of the vessel not under command. Choice D: Both vessels are required to take action to stay clear of each other.
response: Choice C: The fishing vessel must keep out of the way of the vessel not under command.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Of the vessels listed, which must keep out of the way of all the others?
Choice A: A vessel constrained by her draft Choice B: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice C: A vessel pushing a barge Choice D: A vessel engaged in fishing
response: Choice C: A vessel pushing a barge

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which vessel shall avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft?
Choice A: A vessel not under command Choice B: A sailing vessel Choice C: A vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice B: A sailing vessel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A signal of intent must be sounded in international waters by _______________________.
Choice A: a vessel meeting another head-on Choice B: a vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel Choice C: a vessel crossing the course of another Choice D: the give-way vessel in a crossing situation
response: Choice B: a vessel overtaking another in a narrow channel

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be an ________________.
Choice A: all-round yellow light only Choice B: all-round white light only Choice C: all-round blue light only Choice D: alternating red and yellow light
response: Choice B: all-round white light only

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is TRUE, according§to the Rules?
Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver. Choice B: A vessel not under command shall keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver. Choice C: A fishing vessel while underway has the right-of-way over a vessel constrained by her draft. Choice D: A vessel not under command shall avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft.
response: Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be an _____.
Choice A: all-round white or yellow light Choice B: all-round yellow light only Choice C: all-round white light only Choice D: Any colored light is acceptable.
response: Choice C: all-round white light only

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is TRUE, according§to the Rules?
Choice A: A vessel constrained by her draft shall keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing. Choice B: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver. Choice C: A vessel not under command shall avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft. Choice D: A vessel not under command shall keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.
response: Choice B: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is TRUE, according to§the Rules?
Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver. Choice B: A vessel not under command shall keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver. Choice C: A vessel engaged in fishing shall keep out of the way of a sailing vessel. Choice D: A vessel not under command shall keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing.
response: Choice A: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY Which statement is TRUE, according§to the Rules?
Choice A: A vessel not under command shall keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver. Choice B: A vessel not under command shall avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft. Choice C: A vessel constrained by her draft shall keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing. Choice D: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.
response: Choice D: A vessel engaged in fishing while underway shall, so far as possible, keep out of the way of a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY What characteristic must a light have if used to signal passing intentions?
Choice A: It must be an all-round white light. Choice B: It must be an alternating blue and white light. Choice C: It must be an all-round white or yellow light. Choice D: It must be an alternating red and yellow light.
response: Choice A: It must be an all-round white light.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY What characteristic must a light used to indicate passing intentions have?
Choice A: It must be an alternating red and yellow light. Choice B: It must be an all-round white light. Choice C: It must be an all-round yellow light. Choice D: It must be an all-round blue light.
response: Choice B: It must be an all-round white light.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A power-driven vessel pushing ahead§or towing alongside will show sidelights, a sternlight, and _____________________.
Choice A: an all-round red light where it can best be seen Choice B: two yellow masthead lights in a vertical line Choice C: two masthead lights in a vertical line Choice D: a single white light forward
response: Choice C: two masthead lights in a vertical line
